Florida State Seminoles Louisville Cardinals NCAAF Louisville looks to get back on track following a second straight loss in ACC play when it hosts Florida State at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium tonight at 7 p.m. ET (ESPN). The Cardinals are 4.5-point home favorites, but my Florida State vs. Louisville predictions and college football picks for Friday, Oct. 9 expect the Seminoles' offense to take advantage of one of the country's worst defenses. Who will win Florida State vs Louisville: Florida State +4.5 Florida State is coming off a narrative-changing victory after beating Virginia by 31 points. The Seminoles have now covered in each of their last two games against FBS opponents, showcasing one of the country's best run games. With Ashton Daniels at QB and Ousmane Kromah at running back, FSU is 12th nationally in EPA per rush and 17th in rush success rate (49.7%). That could be a problem for a Louisville defense that's been one of the worst in the Power Four, allowing the 14th-most yards per game in the country (423). Daniels and Kromah have combined for 755 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns in five games, and if they get going on the ground, Florida State can turn this into a shootout on the road. I like FSU at +3.5 or better . TOP PICK Florida State vs Louisville Over/Under pick: Over 59.5 Louisville has an offense that looks capable of winning the ACC and a defense that looks capable of losing every game against a quality opponent. In four FBS games, Louisville has averaged 33.5 points per game and allowed 33.2 ppg. The Cardinals have hit the Over in three of those games, and I like them to do it again with a total of 60.5 or better . With Lincoln Kienholz expected to be healthy for Louisville, he should keep the offense humming. The Cardinals rank top 25 nationally in offensive success rate (49.7%) , and Kienholz has accounted for 15 touchdowns and a 77.2 QBR. Kienholz, along with running back Isaac Brown (and Keyjuan Brown if he plays), should push a Florida State defense that's 98th in rush success rate (46.9%) and 93rd in net adjusted EPA per play. Florida State vs Louisville combo Louisville's defense is the reason it's already lost three games this season and why it's failed to cover in two straight ACC matchups. Louisville doesn't create negative plays on defense, ranking third-last in the ACC in havoc rate (13.2%) and 88th in net EPA per play. With Kromah and Daniels carrying FSU's ground attack, they will be able to break loose for big plays and approach 30+ points. Meanwhile, FSU has defensive issues of its own, ranking 92nd in available yards percentage (52.1%) . A high-scoring game should lead to a back-and-forth final frame. Florida State +4.5 Florida State vs Louisville prop: Florida State team total Over 27.5 Florida State has scored 28+ points in four of five games this season, and Louisville has allowed 28+ points to all four of its FBS opponents this season. I'd play the Over on the Seminoles' team total at 27.5 or better . The Seminoles are averaging 33.2 ppg this season, and Kromah has quickly become one of the best running backs in the country. He ranks top 10 nationally in forced missed tackles on runs (28) and runs of 10+ yards (14). Daniels' mobility has opened up the offense, too, with the Auburn transfer sitting top 25 in the country in QBR (80.5) thanks to the damage he's doing on the ground. Final prediction for Florida State vs. Louisville in a big Week 6 meeting
picks.blurb: Final prediction for Florida State vs. Louisville in a big Week 6 meeting Skip to main content Recruiting Women's sports Men's basketball Women's basketball Baseball & softball FanSided NCAA Sites Florida State is just a few hours away from kicking off Week 6 against the Louisville Cardinals in Kentucky. The Seminoles managed to improve to 3-2 last week in a major way, and the win allowed fans to enjoy Florida State football for a moment. Now, the next challenge awaits, and Louisville is a far different team compared to Virginia. Last week, Florida State entered the game as home underdogs against Virginia, and the team appeared to take that personally based on the response on the field. The Seminoles shifted the momentum of the game in the second quarter and never looked back afterwards. Securing a dominant win always feels good, but the reality is that Florida State still has plenty of work to do moving forward. Hosting the Seminoles this week will be the Cardinals, who are in the middle of a two-game losing streak against the likes of NC State and Wake Forest. Empty possessions have not been a problem for Louisville, but fumbles and the growing miscommunications on defense have. The talent is certainly there, but the results have not been, which makes Louisville a very dangerous team to play against. Can Florida State replicate the Week 5 success against Louisville? The expectations have now been set for Florida State after coach Mike Norvell proved this team can win dominantly. Now, the real test begins, and that involves repeating that performance against another strong ACC team in Louisville. It might be a rough start to the season for Louisville at 2-3, but the Cardinals' team is loaded with talent, particularly on the offensive side. Quarterback Lincoln Kienholz looked like a true Heisman Trophy candidate early and remains a very dangerous player despite the recent losses. Louisville is arguably the only team in the ACC that could potentially rival Miami offensively, and they will serve as a serious test for the Florida State defense. Virginia is a very experienced team, and Florida State found a way to shut them down on offense, but Louisville is not necessarily the same type of team. Kienholz and the Cardinals hurt opposing defenses through the air, which happens to be an area of weakness for Florida State. Expect a long night for both defenses during Week 6 Completely shutting down the Cardinals' offense is likely not going to happen, as the worst performance the offense had this season was good for 399 total yards and 27 points. The Louisville offense is a different animal, and that could pose a threat to the Florida State defense and the secondary in particular. With that in mind, Louisville could certainly have an explosive day on offense, but there is also a good chance that Florida State does the same. The Cardinals have the second-worst defense in the ACC, with an average of 29.2 points per game allowed. Louisville additionally allows 423 total yards per game, which means moving the football into scoring position should not be an issue for Florida State. Florida State has looked better defensively over the past two games, allowing an average of 226.5 total yards gained. The defense should be able to find enough success to prevent a blowout, but this game will likely come down to who makes the last mistake on offense. Prediction: Florida State 38, Louisville 35 Loading recommendations... The Seminoles are without key receivers and defensive backs, while the Cardinals have their starting quarterback listed as probable. The Seminoles are dealing with a long list of players who will not be available. Running back Samuel Singleton Jr. is out, along with wide receiver Devin Carter. These absences force coach Mike Norvell to shuffle his depth chart significantly before kickoff. On the positive side, linebacker Mikai Gbayor and Karon Maycock are probable. The Cardinals also have defensive back Koen Entringer and lineman AJ Green listed as probable. However, they are without defensive back Antonio Watts and tight end Travis Egan. Starting quarterback Lincoln Kienholz's status is the biggest story for Louisville fans heading into the game. The Cardinals are also missing several other key players. Running back Keyjuan Brown is questionable, along with offensive lineman Cason Henry. Defensive lineman Daylen Russell is also in the questionable group. picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska Football vs. Indiana Preview & Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska is getting ready for a huge Big Ten matchup against Indiana, and Adam Carriker breaks down what the Huskers have to do if they want to pull off the upset and earn some serious respect. This is one of those games that can change the way people look at a team. Nebraska has put together a strong start, but now the Huskers get a chance to prove it against a ranked Indiana team led by Curt Cignetti. Indiana has been one of the best teams in the Big Ten, and this game will give Matt Rhule’s team a chance to show how far it has come. Carriker starts by looking back at the history between Nebraska and Indiana; he then shifts to Nebraska’s offense and quarterback Anthony Colandrea. If Nebraska is going to win this game, Colandrea will need to have a big day. He has to make smart decisions, take care of the football, and make plays with both his arm and his legs. Carriker also compares Colandrea to Indiana’s quarterback Josh Hoover and talks about why Nebraska needs to put pressure on Hoover and force him into mistakes. The Huskers’ pass catchers are another major part of the matchup. Nebraska has playmakers who can make a difference, and Carriker takes a closer look at players like Kwazi Gilmer and how they match up with Indiana’s defense. On the other side of the ball, Nebraska’s defense could be one of the biggest factors in the game. Rob Aurich and the Nebraska defense will need to be at their best, especially on third down. Indiana has talented receivers, solid running backs, and an offense that can hurt teams in several different ways. Nebraska cannot afford to give up easy conversions or big plays. One of the biggest topics in the episode is penalties. Nebraska had 16 penalties last week while Indiana had zero. That is a massive difference, and Carriker makes it clear that Nebraska cannot expect to beat a ranked team if it keeps hurting itself. Cleaning up the penalties is one of his biggest keys to the game. Carriker wraps up the show by laying out five keys for Nebraska: limit penalties, stop the run, play four full quarters, run the football, and limit big plays. None of those things are complicated, but Nebraska has to do all five if it wants to compete and win. The Huskers also need to be ready for a physical game. Carriker talks about trading blows with Indiana and matching the Hoosiers for all four quarters. This cannot be a game where Nebraska plays well for two or three quarters and then fades late. The second half will be huge. Carriker also throws in a little extra motivation with a beard bet if Nebraska wins. At the end of the show, he gives his final score prediction: Indiana 27, Nebraska 24. He sees it as a close game, but Nebraska will need a big performance from Colandrea, a strong game from the defense, and much cleaner football to pull off the upset. Learn inside info first, only on the Carriker Chronicles. Stay up to date on all things Huskers by bookmarking Nebraska Cornhuskers On SI , subscribing to HuskerMax on YouTube and visiting HuskerMax.com daily. Loading recommendations... Please wait while we load personalized content recommendations ADAM CARRIKER Adam’s dream of playing for the Huskers came to fruition. He was twice named first-team All-Big 12, leading the conference in sacks and winning the Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year award his senior season, along with several other awards, including finishing with All-America honors, in addition to being named to the Big 12 Commissioner’s Academic Honor Roll three times. He’s also been named to Nebraska’s All-Century Team, voted The Best Husker Defensive End since the start of the new millennium, and has been inducted into the Nebraska Football Hall of Fame. Adam went on to play eight years as a Defensive Lineman in the NFL with the St. Louis Rams and Washington Redskins. He was drafted in the 1st round, winning Rams Rookie of the Year; he’s the only Ram in franchise history to start all 16 games as a rookie. He also won the Strongest Redskin award multiple times during his career in the NFL. Since retiring, he’s experienced great success in the business world and has also appeared multiple times on National Television and Radio Shows, and currently hosts his highly popular show, the Carriker Chronicles, aka, the People’s Show, which has been viewed by millions! As they continue their quest for a second-consecutive title, the Hoosiers faced their most difficult task yet this season this weekend — but still managed to pass. Watch select college football games live with Fubo (free trial) A pair of fourth-quarter touchdown passes from Josh Hoover to Nick Marsh keyed a late comeback for Indiana , which rebounded from an 11-point deficit to defeat Nebraska , 20-17, on Saturday, Oct. 10 at Memorial Stadium in Lincoln, Nebraska. The victory extended the Hoosiers' FBS-leading win streak to 22 games and improve their record this season to 6-0. The Cornhuskers , meanwhile, fell to 5-1 despite leading for much of the game. REQUIRED READING: Is Indiana football underrated? Biases, data inform poll voters. Here's what matters Nebraska looked to be in position for a signature win in its fourth season under coach Matt Rhule , with a 17-6 lead with 12 minutes remaining in the fourth quarter after a 39-yard Anthony Colandrea touchdown run. On the first play of Indiana's ensuing drive, though, Hoover found Marsh over the middle for a 75-yard touchdown pass to get within four, 17-13. After forcing a Nebraska punt, the Hoosiers were faced with a fourth-and-1 at the Huskers' 44-yard line. Indiana faked the run against a Nebraska defense selling out to stop the short gain and Hoover found a wide-open Marsh for a touchdown with 7:13 remaining. Marsh finished with 187 receiving yards and two touchdowns on six catches, accounting for the vast majority of Hoover's 263 passing yards. In a losing effort, Colandrea had 302 total yards and a touchdown. With Saturday's result, Nebraska has lost 31 consecutive games against ranked opponents. away.headline: Riley Van Poppel injury threatens Nebraska where Indiana can hurt it most
away.blurb: Considering that Van Poppel looked like he wasn't adjusting all that well to Aurich's defense in fall camp and then surged into a situation where he was getting as many snaps as any defensive lineman in the last few weeks, it couldn't be a worse time for an injury to keep him out of Saturday morning's massive game. The good for Nebraska heading into the massive showdown against Indiana on Saturday is that the team is mostly healthy. Jamal Rule, Jacory Barney, and Mekhi Nelson are off the injury reports entirely. The bad news is that Thursday night's report added a defensive player the Huskers can scarcely afford to miss. Riley Van Poppel's apparent injury isn't a big deal simply because he's a defensive lineman, and the Hoosiers' run game is easily the best the Huskers have faced so far this year. His potential absence is also a big issue because Van Poppel's playing time has increased as the season has gone on. Van Poppel's use by Nebraska defensive coordinator Rob Aurich has, in fact, never been bigger than it has been since Nebraska started Big Ten play. Against Ohio, he saw just 30 snaps. Against Bowling Green, it was down to 18, and he had just 28 snaps against North Dakota. However, he tallied 46 snaps against Michigan State and 44last week against Maryland. Riley Van Poppel injury could weaken Nebraska football front against Indiana running backs Van Poppel hasn't always been on the stat sheet. He has just 7 tackles, but 2 of those were sacks. He's also got 9 quarterback pressures, including 5 in Big Ten games alone. While his 2 sacks came in non-conference play, he's shown he can make an impact in the trenches, with 2 quarterback hurries and a quarterback hit against the Spartans and 2 more hurries against the Terrapins. "I think I'm playing probably the best I have in four years right now," Van Poppel said after Nebraska's Week 4 win over Michigan State . Van Poppel has also been a vocal leader for Nebraska, especially after earning a single-digit jersey last year and being given the option of keeping it this fall. Instead of once again wearing No. 5, he went back to his No. 44, saying he didn't believe he lived up to his own standard of what a player wearing a single digit jersey should be like. “He (Rhule) gave me the option to keep one, but I don’t see it that way. I want the guys who were truly voted to be the single digits, and if I need to go back to a different number, at the end of the day, it’s a number.” As is the policy with the Big Ten Availability Reports, it's not a guarantee that Riley Van Poppel will miss Nebraska's biggest game of the year. The Huskers will release two more before game time. One report will update the status of injured players on Friday night, and another two hours before kickoff. away.blurb: The biggest bit of good news from this week's initial availability report is that cornerback AJ Harris is not featured. Harris, a transfer from Penn State, went down in Week 1 against North Texas and hasn't been able to return to the field since. Harris has 35 appearances with 27 starts under his belt after one season at Georgia and two at Penn State. He came to Bloomington after an impressive junior season that saw him earn All-Big Ten defensive honorable mention recognition with the Nittany Lions in 2025. Jaylen Bell has played well in Harris' absence, but it seems that Harris now full-go for Week 6. Defensive lineman Daniel Ndukwe is also off this week's availability report after missing Week 5 against Rutgers. His return brings even more depth and talent to Indiana's dangerous defensive front. The lone Hoosier RB still sidelined is Khobie Martin, which doesn't come as a surprise as he continues to nurse a broken forearm that he suffered in Week 1. WR Lebron Bond has also been upgraded to questionable for Saturday's matchup against Rutgers. The absences of Martin and Williams are expected, leaving the Hoosiers with few injury surprises at this time. The lone downside is Andrew Barker being ruled out. He was injured against Rutgers and won't be able suit up for the Nebraska game. All things considered, this initial Week 6 injury report brings plenty of good news for the Hoosiers. Five players have been ruled out for Week 6 for the Cornhuskers: WR Larry Miles, DB Kahmir Prescott, LB Jase Reynolds, LB Jacob Bower, and DL Gabe Moore. Two other Cornhuskers, TE Carter Nelson and LB Gage Stenger are listed as doubtful. Kick-off betwen Indiana and Nebraska is set for Noon ET on Saturday afternoon. The Indiana Hoosiers have been dealing with some key injuries throughout the past couple of weeks. But even with some reliable contributors sidelined, Indiana has been able to cruise to a 5-0 record to start the season. However, the competition is about to increase substantially the rest of the way. The Hoosiers travel to Lincoln to take on undefeated Nebraska in Week 6, and with matchups against Ohio State, Michigan, USC, and Washington still looming, getting as healthy as possible is of the utmost importance for Curt Cignetti and company. home.headline: Riley Van Poppel injury threatens Nebraska where Indiana can hurt it most
home.blurb: Considering that Van Poppel looked like he wasn't adjusting all that well to Aurich's defense in fall camp and then surged into a situation where he was getting as many snaps as any defensive lineman in the last few weeks, it couldn't be a worse time for an injury to keep him out of Saturday morning's massive game. The good for Nebraska heading into the massive showdown against Indiana on Saturday is that the team is mostly healthy. Jamal Rule, Jacory Barney, and Mekhi Nelson are off the injury reports entirely. The bad news is that Thursday night's report added a defensive player the Huskers can scarcely afford to miss. Riley Van Poppel's apparent injury isn't a big deal simply because he's a defensive lineman, and the Hoosiers' run game is easily the best the Huskers have faced so far this year. His potential absence is also a big issue because Van Poppel's playing time has increased as the season has gone on. Van Poppel's use by Nebraska defensive coordinator Rob Aurich has, in fact, never been bigger than it has been since Nebraska started Big Ten play. Against Ohio, he saw just 30 snaps. Against Bowling Green, it was down to 18, and he had just 28 snaps against North Dakota. However, he tallied 46 snaps against Michigan State and 44last week against Maryland. Riley Van Poppel injury could weaken Nebraska football front against Indiana running backs Van Poppel hasn't always been on the stat sheet. He has just 7 tackles, but 2 of those were sacks. He's also got 9 quarterback pressures, including 5 in Big Ten games alone. While his 2 sacks came in non-conference play, he's shown he can make an impact in the trenches, with 2 quarterback hurries and a quarterback hit against the Spartans and 2 more hurries against the Terrapins. "I think I'm playing probably the best I have in four years right now," Van Poppel said after Nebraska's Week 4 win over Michigan State . Van Poppel has also been a vocal leader for Nebraska, especially after earning a single-digit jersey last year and being given the option of keeping it this fall. Instead of once again wearing No. 5, he went back to his No. 44, saying he didn't believe he lived up to his own standard of what a player wearing a single digit jersey should be like. “He (Rhule) gave me the option to keep one, but I don’t see it that way. I want the guys who were truly voted to be the single digits, and if I need to go back to a different number, at the end of the day, it’s a number.” As is the policy with the Big Ten Availability Reports, it's not a guarantee that Riley Van Poppel will miss Nebraska's biggest game of the year. The Huskers will release two more before game time. One report will update the status of injured players on Friday night, and another two hours before kickoff. Arizona (4-1, 1-1 in Big 12) now heads out to the country roads of West Virginia, where they will face a high-scoring Mountaineers squad in the midst of a two-game losing streak. West Virginia bullied then No. 25 Virginia, 38-27, in Week 3 to build momentum heading into Big 12 play. Things haven't gone well for coach Rich Rodriguez's team since then, however, with an ugly 41-24 home loss to Oklahoma State followed by a shootout at Iowa State that ended in a 45-42 defeat after Cyclones running back Aiden Flora scored his fifth touchdown with 1:57 left in the fourth quarter. Meet the Mountaineers Iowa State linebacker Sullivan Schlimgen (7) takes down West Virginia quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. (3) | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Cincinnati presented a challenge for Arizona's run defense, a challenge the Wildcats more than met after holding the Bearcats to a season-low 87 yards on the ground. Cincinnati presented a challenge for Arizona's run defense, a challenge the Wildcats more than met after holding the Bearcats to a season-low 87 yards on the ground. Now they'll level up against the best rushing attack in the country. WVU has 1,470 rushing yards on the season, which not only leads the FBS but is 133 yards more than second place, Army, and 190 yards more than the next high major team in South Carolina. West Virginia's 294 rushing yards per game is third in the FBS, and its 17 rushing touchdowns is tied for third. A big part of the ground attack for the Mountaineers is the dual-threat ability of quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr., who has a whopping 574 rushing yards and 11(!) rushing touchdowns on the season - which is tied with Florida running back Jadan Baugh for the most in the country. Hawkins is good in the air as well, with 836 passing yards and a quality 7:1 touchdown-to-interception ratio through West Virginia's first five games. The good news for Arizona is that West Virginia is about as bad defensively as it is good offensively. The Mountaineers surrender 168.4 rushing yards per game, 108th in the country, and a shockingly bad 288.2 yards per game in the air - 133rd out of 138 FBS teams and only ahead of Stanford among P4 teams. Arizona, even without wideouts Gio Richardson, Chris Hunter, and Tre Spivey, moved the ball quite well against Cincinnati last week, and should have an even easier time doing so on Saturday - even on the road with an early 9:00 AM kickoff. WVU does have some things working in its favor with the Wildcats down key players at the skill positions in addition to playing abnormally early by their standards. ESPN's Bill Connelly's SP+ model doesn't think it will be enough, though, for the Mountaineers to get back in the win column, projecting a 34-24 victory for the visitors. I'm sorry...what??? West Virginia University Football | Christopher Hall - West Virginia on SI Look, I can fully understand Arizona being the projected winner, but only a combined 58 points? I'm not so sure about that. Yes, the Wildcats have been good against the run, but their blitz-happy nature makes them vulnerable to explosive plays in the passing game, which WVU has hit on consistently all year. And while they do have the 11th-ranked run defense in the country, they haven't quite seen a rushing attack like the one they will face on Saturday in Morgantown, which averages just a shade under 295 yards per game. The Mountaineers will move the ball and score points, just like Arizona will. If the final score ends up 34-24, I'd see it actually going WVU's way, believe it or not. This would likely mean that the Mountaineers are able to force a couple of turnovers, and the absence of Tre Spivey, Chris Hunter III, and Gio Richardson impacts Arizona's ability to be as potent through the air. Again, I don't see that being the case, just like I don't expect West Virginia to be held to just 24 points. What a loss would mean for the Mountaineers West Virginia University quarterback Mike Hawkins Jr. | Christopher Hall - West Virginia on SI Dropping to 3-3 is far from ideal, especially when you look at the remainder of the schedule - games against TCU and Texas Tech on the road, Houston comes to Morgantown, and then a road trip to Utah to end the year. Not to mention, going to TCU won't be easy. I'll keep saying it, though: With the way this offense moves the ball and puts it into the end zone, it makes the schedule not nearly as daunting as it may be with a shaky unit to go along with a struggling defense. There may be games that the Mountaineers win that they are not expected to because of that offense, and this weekend against the Wildcats could be one of them. picks.blurb: West Virginia football expert previews the Arizona game, makes a score prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football winners/losers Oklahoma stuns Texas Marvin Harrison Jr. getting traded Valkyries finish sweep Angel Reese: Finals Barbie AMES, IA - OCTOBER 3: Head coach Rich Rodriguez of the West Virginia Mountaineers shakes hands with quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. #3 of the West Virginia Mountaineers celebrating a Mountaineers touchdown in the first half of play against the Iowa State Cyclones at Jack Trice Stadium on October 3, 2026, in Ames, Iowa. (Photo by David Purdy/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brian Pedersen Tue, October 6, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's not just Game Week, it's RichRod Game Week! Arizona's first trip to West Virginia will see it face off against former head coach Rich Rodriguez , who is back with the Mountaineers for a second go-around. Rodriguez coached there from 2001-07 before going to Michigan for three years and then spending 2012-17 with the Wildcats. The current West Virginia team is on a 2-game skid, losing a 45-42 shootout at Iowa State last weekend after falling at home to Oklahoma State in its Big 12 opener. To better understand RichRod's squad, we reached out to Dillon Clark of SB Nation sister site The Smoking Musket for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his impressive answers to our mediocre questions: AZ Desert Swarm: West Virginia went 3-0 in nonconference play, including an impressive win over Virginia, but then has lost both conference games. What have been the main contributing factors to the backslide? Dillon Clark: "There has been a significant increase in competition in Big 12 play compared to our nonconference schedule. The win against Virginia looked good at the time because they were ranked, but after their performance against Florida State last week I don't think they are going to be anywhere near the top of the ACC again. Our defense hasn't looked great all year but the wheels have come completely off in the last two games. We have given up over 1,200 yards of total offense in the last two games which equates to about 3/4 of a mile if you were wondering." It's to no one's surprise in Wildcat Nation that a RichRod-coached team is running the ball well, but this production seems to be at another level. What's been the key to the rushing success, and how do you think Arizona's defense will try to neutralize this? "We spent a ton of money in the portal on a quarterback, running back and several offensive linemen. Michael Hawkins Jr. has exceeded expectations at the quarterback position for us averaging over 100 yards per game on the ground 6.2 yards per carry. Many of his best runs are coming off of pass plays that would have resulted in a sack or throw away for most other QBs so when you turn those negative plays into big positives it really shows up on the stat sheet. One of the biggest surprises to me has been his elusiveness in the red zone and the ability to make people miss. I knew he was fast, I didn't realize how shifty he is. Cam Cook has also produced at a high level in the RB position. He is such a tough runner. His yards after contact and broken tackles are what really sets him apart. Even though he isn't what I would call fast, he has consistently popped big runs. He gets stronger as the game goes on and the majority of his yardage has come in the second half of games." Quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. is tied for the FBS lead with 11 rushing touchdowns, but how is he as a passer? Would you trust him if he had to be one-dimensional in this way? "I think it's fair to call Michael Hawkins Jr. a streaky passer. The last three games he has started out looking a bit shaky in the pass game with off target throws. In two of the three he eventually settled in and made plays with his arm. The completion percentage against Iowa State was a bit lower than you like, but he did have a couple drops and throw aways in there. I have confidence in him as a passer, my bigger question is can our receivers get open consistently in a situation where we have to throw the ball, and can we establish an intermediate passing game? It feels like our passing game at times this year has been all or nothing. The drive-extending, possession-style passing game has not been sharp. I don't blame that on Michael Hawkins as much as I do on play calling and scheme. I have a hard time seeing anyone making him purely one dimensional as a passer this year. Teams may shut down our traditional running game, but we have seen teams put multiple spies on him in the past few weeks and he is still escaping the pocket for chunk yardage." The Mountaineers' defensive numbers are not good, ranking last in the Big 12 in almost every category. Is this a talent issue, a problem with the scheme, or both? "In order to be as bad as we have been, it has to be all of the above right? Our tackling is bad. Missed assignments on nearly every possession.We can't get pressure on the quarterback. When we are in the right place we end up with a pass interference penalty. It's rough all around. There has been a lot of talk on if Zac Alley's reputation as a sort of 'mad scientist' on defense could be part of the problem. It's really hard to argue against that when you see us consistently confused on pre-snap alignments. The biggest concern is that we are struggling in every aspect. Scoring defense, rushing defense, pass defense, total yardage, it doesn't matter which stat you look at, we are at or near the bottom. The only hope is that potentially our two best defenders just became eligible last week. Jacorey Thomas and Jason Chambers should help plug some holes in what has been a leaky secondary. There is only one way for us to go from here." How has the second coming of RichRod been so far in your estimation? Have there been any classic moments in terms of his antics? "After the Virginia win in Week 3 the vibes around the WVU fan base were as high as I've seen them in a very long time. That game brought back a lot of great memories from Rich Rod's first tenure here and it felt like the sky was the limit. The last two weeks have put a damper on the mood though the fact that the offense has been producing at a high level still does take some of the blame off of him. The Rich Rod offense is back and it's humming, but how did he not see this coming with the defense? There was definitely a group of the fanbase that didn't want him back, and those voices are getting louder with each loss. I think he has shown enough so far that the majority of the fan base still believes he can get this right. We love that he holds players accountable in the moment, and it gives us hope that he can turn this thing around." Prediction time. Does Arizona beat its former coach and get a big conference road win or do the Mountaineers hold serve at home? Give us a score prediction. "We have the worst defense in the Big 12. You have one of the best offenses. We are coming off of two straight brutal conference losses. You are coming off of a dominant win against a previously undefeated Cincinnati team. In other words, we have you right where we want you. 45-31 Mountaineers get back on track at home."

Antwan Roberts, Quincy Craig and Kedrick Reescano each had scoring runs for the Wildcats (5-1, 2-1), who won their fourth straight despite missing their top three wide receivers, all who were injured a week ago in a win over Cincinnati . With a potent offense like Arizona coming to Morgantown, you'd like to be at full strength defensively, but it looks like the Mountaineers will be down a starter, with arguably their top corner, Nick Taylor, downgraded from questionable to doubtful. The good news is that pass rusher Harper Holloman, who battled through a banged-up shoulder last week at Iowa State, is trending to be in uniform this Saturday. Arizona's offensive line has not been great in pass protection this season, giving up 15 sacks this year, which ranks 126th nationally - a great sight for a defense that has struggled to manufacture pressure since the start of league play. Having Holloman, the Mountaineers' best pass rusher available, is a big, big deal. When Noah Fifita is kept clean, he's completing nearly 80% of his passes for over 1,100 yards and 12 touchdowns. This is the one guy you can't allow to stand in the pocket and pick you apart. Who fills in for Taylor if he's downgraded to OUT? Keyshawn Robinson will likely still be a part of the rotation there, and maybe even Jaire Rawlison as well, who has seen limited action so far this season. The next availability report will need to be submitted by 10 p.m. ET tonight, and if Taylor is still considered doubtful, it at least gives a sliver of hope that he can go or at least be available. Mandatory Credit: Danny Wild-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Doug Joubert Thu, October 8, 2026 at 3:50 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Tulane 2026 Football Schedule 6:30PM, 10/16 In a battle of colors Saturday morning in West Point, the Tulane Green Wave open the defense of their American Conference 2025 championship by visiting the Army Black Knights. Both teams enter the contest at 2-2 on the season. Team Schedules The Wave has lost its road contests against ACC defending champion Duke to open the season, then versus Big-12 opponent Kansas State two weeks later. Sandwiched between and after the two trips were home contests against Sun Belt teams, which Tulane claimed victories in both: South Alabama in the home opener and Southern Miss two weeks ago. The Green Wave had an open date last Saturday before its conference opener this weekend. Army opened the season at home with a 56-point shellacking of Bryant University out of the Coastal Athletic. The Black Knights followed with an American Conference loss at Michie Stadium versus South Florida, an early open date, then a league victory at Temple before falling at Louisiana Tech last weekend. See the PFF comparisons between Army and Tulane here. The Black Knights opened a 3.5-point favorite over the Green Wave earlier this week. That number has dropped to 3-point Army advantage since Monday. As of this writing, 81% of the money bet is on Army, giving the points to Tulane. Tulane Has Something to Prove: Our On SI Tulane Prognostication This 2026 version of Green Wave football has, if anything, been consistently inconsistent. Open the season with your new starting quarterback, who is replaced after 30-minutes, whose replacement is replaced a little over two-and-half games later, and whose replacement of the replacement is replaced for one play. Show an erratic rushing offense that can slash opponents with gigantic games from various running backs, but have nothing on a regular basis . Big passing plays to big players, but with drops and throws that sometimes don't come close, showing communication and concentration issues. Offensive and defensive fronts that are growing and progressing, but is their growth rate fast enough? Stop an opponent with three-and-outs on defense on consecutive drives, then have huge rushing gaps open in the defensive front seven or wide open receivers in the secondary. To have this much variety in results is confusing and awkward. There is plenty of talent on this team. With 60-returnees from the 2025 playoff team and some solid additions, think Jaylin Lucas, Fat Hill, Macho Stephenson, Ed Smith IV , this team should be hitting stride. But it's not. Instead, it is showing how consistently inconsistent it can be, which you cannot do against a team like Army. The Black Knights are the least penalized team in the American Conference only getting 16-flags on the season. They are the 5th least in all the NCAA. They do not make mistakes. If you are inconsistent, the discipline of Army will expose that, and expose it quickly. No matter how much coaches and players talk about defending the Black Knights option, it's another thing to actually do it. To defend it will take that word we keep on bringing up: consistency. We have not seen that from this Tulane team this year. They have to prove that they can be a team that does things well and does them on a regular basis. They have yet to do so. We think the big play will be open for Tulane, as the Black Knights give up more yards per play than any other team in the American, almost 7-yards a pop. If the Wave offensive front is able to open the holes for the running back and protect the quarterback, whoever that may be (we believe it should be Trace Johnson , but we've been wrong before), there will be big chunks available. However, we also believe Army's multiple option attack will be the undoing of the Green Wave defense. On SI Tulane Pick: Army 35 - Tulane 28 Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Tulane Green Wave at Army Black Knights Prediction, Picks & Odds for Week 6
2026 Week 6 Preview: Tulane Green Wave @ Army Black Knights
picks.blurb: 2026 Week 6 Preview: Tulane Green Wave @ Army Black Knights | Underdog Dynasty Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Rest of the FBS Community Underdog Dynasty October 11, 2026 Underdog Dynasty Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Conference USA Sun Belt Conference American Athletic Conference Betting FanDuel College Football Odds College Football Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Conference USA Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications American Conference Two high-powered rushing attacks meet in West Point for the first time since the 2024 American title game. Time and date: Saturday, October 10 at 12:00 p.m. ET Network: CBS Sports Network Location: Michie Stadium — West Point, NY Spread: Army (-3.5) Over/under: 48.5 All-time series: Tulane leads, 14-10-1 Last meeting: Tulane 24, Army 17 — October 18, 2025 Current streak: Tulane, 1 (2025) Setting the scene Even before sharing the American Conference, Army and Tulane were famliar opponents, squaring off 19 times from 1996 through 2020. The Black Knights then joined the American in 2024 and instantly ran the league, rattling off an 8-0 conference record before handling Tulane in the conference championship game. That was the only time in the last four years Tulane didn’t serve as the conference title host. With first-year head coach Will Hall in the fold, the Green Wave hope to host the American Championship for a fourth time in five years. To achieve that goal, it starts with defeating Army at Michie Stadium in this conference opener. Tulane Green Wave outlook Tulane (2-2, 0-0 American) split its non-conference slate, falling to Duke and Kansas State by double-digits on the road, while escaping Sun Belt opponents South Alabama and Southern Miss at home with late fourth quarter heroics. The biggest question entering this game, asks: who starts at quarterback? Zeon Chriss-Gremillion was Tulane’s Week 1 starter, but the Green Wave moved to Kadin Semonza for Weeks 2 through 4. But at the end of the last outing against Southern Miss, head coach Will Hall changed quarterbacks from Semonza to true freshman Trace Johnson in the fourth quarter. Johnson provided a spark in the come-from-behind victory, but his sample size remains small, completing just 2-of-5 passes for 35 yards without a single rushing attempt. The passing game unquestionably needs a boost. Tulane ranks 105th in the FBS in passing offense, completing just 54.2 percent of attempts with three touchdowns against one interception. The pass protection has been lacking too, allowing the 11th-most sacks per game in the country at 3.3. However, the Green Wave can dominate on the ground, and they do it with several different weapons. Running backs Jaylin Lucas and Maurice Turner each rushed for 200+ yards in the first four weeks, and the group gets even deeper as Jamauri McClure — Tulane’s starting running back during its 2025 College Football Playoff run — is slated to make his season debut. Tulane’s strength last season was its run defense, but the Green Wave have fallen off in that department, entering this matchup against the No. 1 rushing offense ranked 125th — allowing 191 yards per game on the ground. Losing star outside linebacker Chris Rodgers certainly doesn’t help, but the Green Wave still present veteran linebackers Makai Williams and Dickson Agu, who will be essential to countering this option. Army Black Knights outlook Army (2-2, 1-1 American) is already preparing for its third conference game. The Black Knights’ first two conference matchups were decided by the thinnest margins, featuring a lead change in the final two minutes. Army wound up on the wrong side of that late lead change in Week 2 when South Florida converted a late fourth down for a game-winning touchdown. But two weeks later, the Black Knights returned the favor at Temple. One-score games are customary for Army. Nine of the Black Knights’ last 10 matchups against FBS competition were decided by one score, and eight of the last nine were decided by four points or fewer — including every FBS matchup this season. Army’s option offense is in a familiar spot at first in the country in rushing yards per game at 334, while averaging the sixth-most yards per carry (6.4) in the FBS. Cale Hellums, who led all quarterbacks in rushing last year, remains the unit’s leading rusher with 301 yards, and his rushing performance dictates the result more than anyone else. In Army’s two wins, he has 191 yards and five touchdowns on a 6.6 average. In the losses to South Florida and Louisiana Tech, he combined for 110 yards and one touchdown on a 3.0 average. The Black Knights’ other ball carriers in the option attack include running back Godspower Nwawuihe and the explosive slot backs Samari Howard (293 rushing yards on a 10.9 average) and Zach Mundell (159 yards on a 14.5 average). However, Nwawuihe’s status remains unknown after he missed the Louisiana Tech game, which could make Carson Smith and Jake Rendina the downhill threats. Army’s defense allowed over 500 yards to Louisiana Tech, and that remains the team’s greatest struggle. The Black Knights are 89th nationally in yards allowed, while playing a style that typically limits possessions. Army has struggled with a lack of backfield pressure, producing the third-fewest sacks (3) and fewest tackles for loss (12) in the country. Additionally, the Black Knights are the only team yet to force a turnover. Army and Tulane are off to somewhat similar starts. Both are 2-2, highlighted by strong ground attacks and run defenses that need improvement. However, they sit on opposite sides of the time of possession spectrum, with Army ranking fourth nationally and Tulane third from the bottom. The Green Wave offense requires explosives in the run game, while the Black Knights move in a more methodical, sustainable fashion. Neither team is a proven passer, and Tulane may lean even more heavily on the run game than usual to keep its defense fresh. As usual, Army games come down to the wire. This will be no exception, and the Black Knights prevail at home in a low-scoring affair. away.headline: Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense
away.blurb: Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense As they practiced on Tuesday for game prep coming off their bye week, Green Wave running back Jamauri McClure was a sight for sore eyes out there, participating in team drills without a non-contact jersey for the first time since he went down with a fractured foot in fall camp. This year's room looks a lot different in comparison. Maurice Turner is playing his best football right now. Jaylin Lucas has gotten some work out in space a bit more this week of prep. Johnnie Daniels has shown that he can throw a killer block as much as he can shoot through a gap. However, the return of McClure is what fans have been clamoring for since the news first got out that he was hurt. Now that he's had ample time to recover, his return should be a major boost for a Tulane offense looking to make the most out of and stretch out what should be expected to be limited possessions against the Army Black Knights Saturday. College football winners/losers Marvin Harrison Jr. getting traded (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Maddy Hudak Tue, October 6, 2026 at 8:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The best ability is often availability, and the Tulane Green Wave certainly have some good news on that front ahead of American conference play. But while head coach Will Hall told media members on Tuesday that he and the team feel that they're a better football team than when we last talked to and saw them last two weeks back, they have a lot to prove on the road to kick off their conference slate. An essential thing they're looking for is an identity on offense. Well, a lot of that can be solved by a strong rush attack that McClure instantaneously boosts. When McClure started taking over the starting running back job towards the end of the year last season, it was clear that he had a different gear and set of traits than what we were seeing from that room. Further good news on that front is that nothing appears to be up with Turner, who ended up limping a bit at the end of his 74-yard touchdown run against the Southern Miss Golden Eagles, as he also was practicing in full with no non-contact jersey. But the true finesse of that room lies with McClure. Another major returnee was wide receiver Zycarl Lewis, who got injured during the season opener against the Duke Blue Devils and hasn't practiced or played since. He was also not in a non-contact jersey on the practice field Tuesday. McClure averaged an impressive 6.5 yards per carry last season. The redshirt sophomore had eight total carries until Week 12 of last year against the FAU Owls. In the final five games of the season, he added 75 touches for 83 total carries for 540 yards and two touchdowns.

away.headline: Army football seeks bounce back in return to home action vs. Tulane
away.blurb: News Sports Life Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals COLLEGE Army football seeks bounce back in return to home action vs. Tulane Ken McMillan Middletown Times Herald- Record Updated Oct. 6, 2026, 9:47 a.m. ET In the end, Army's 21-19 loss at Louisiana Tech on Saturday night was just a non-conference game and didn't affect the American Conference standings. However, the Black Knights are having trouble building on positives. "It's very hard to play perfect,'' said Monken, who also points out the margin for error is slim for his West Point teams. "We're going to strive to it.'' Monken pointed out that Army had too many missed assignments, played with poor fundamentals at times and didn't help themselves with six penalties, but he's not given up on the squad. A dominant win over Bryant in the opener, followed by a crushing late loss at home to South Florida. A tough road win over Temple, followed by a stumbling loss as a small favorite at Louisiana Tech , dropping the Black Knights to 2-2. "We're not going to let this game kind of derail our season,'' said senior center and co-captain Brady Small. "We're going to go back, we're going to watch some film, we're going to learn and get ready for Tulane, another conference game. So just use this as fuel to the fire to get us a win at home.'' Army is a three-point favorite over Tulane for Saturday's noon ET start. Army is 1-1 in American action, and needs a win vs. the Green Wave to stay in contact with the 1-0 leaders: Florida Atlantic (4-1 overall), Memphis (4-1), Texas San Antonio (4-1), Alabama Birmingham (3-2) and North Texas (3-2). Army will face FAU and Memphis but not the other three this season. "Honestly, we've just got to attack the adversity at hand,'' said back Samari Howard. "We can't let this be a lull in our preparation. Overall, we've got to come together as a collective and tackle the adversity and get ready for the next week and the week after that.'' "I don't believe anybody loses momentum unless they stop believing,'' head coach Jeff Monken said. "And I don't think our guys will stop believing. ... If we allow it to derail us, then shame on us. Weve got to learn from it, and each game is independent of the last one. I don't think we allowed last week (win over Temple) to linger into this week. We weren't patting ourselves on the back for such a great job.'' Monken always reminds people that winning college football games is hard. "I love our team,'' he said. "They're tough as nails. They compete, and we played all the way to the end tonight.'' West Point and New Orleans are separated by more than 1,300 miles, but the football programs at Army and Tulane remain very familiar. The Green Wave have a long history with the Black Knights, dating back to 1953 when the two schools battled to a scoreless draw. Next to service academy rivals Navy and Air Force, Army and Tulane have met quite often, 21 times since 1996. Tulane was a founding member of Conference USA in 199

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Brent Venables and the sputtering Sooners face a massive test against Colin Simmons and a dominant Longhorns defense in Dallas Getty Images No. 1 Texas hopes to win the Red River Rivalry matchup against Oklahoma for the third straight time Saturday afternoon at the State Fair of Texas in Dallas. The Longhorns reached No. 1 for the third straight season under Steve Sarkisian, this time after outlasting Ohio State in Week 2. The Longhorns rank among the best defenses in college football , and field quarterback Arch Manning . The Sooners also rank among the best defenses in the sport, but the offense has backslid dramatically under coach Brent Venables. Oklahoma is off to a 2-2 start after a 41-13 loss to No. 2 Georgia last week as the program turned the ball over four times, including a miserable fumble by quarterback John Mateer that was returned for a touchdown. Oklahoma has lost three of four Red River Rivalries under Brent Venables, averaging only 3.0 points per game in those losses. Texas won 23-6 last year as the Sooners turned the ball over three times and were held without a touchdown. Where to watch Texas vs. Oklahoma live Date : Saturday, Oct. 10 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Cotton Bowl -- Dallas TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Texas vs. Oklahoma: Need to know Historically bad offense: Oklahoma's offense has been a disaster through the first several weeks, averaging an astonishing 11.5 points per game against Power Four competition. While quarterback John Mateer has been the primary target, the Sooners are averaging only 2.9 yards per carry, the worst mark in the SEC. Oklahoma failed to score a point against Georgia until trailing 28-0 in the third quarter, and Texas's defense rates higher in many metrics. Rise of Simmons: Texas defensive end Colin Simmons has been regarded as one of the best in the sport, but his performance against Tennessee will go down in the record books. The junior set a Texas record with 5.5 sacks against freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon , which ultimately led to Brandon's benching one week later. Simmons had 29.5 tackles for loss and 21 sacks in his first two seasons, and hopes to build on that as a junior. Which Arch do we get?: Texas quarterback Arch Manning is a lightning rod because of his famous last name, but the junior oscillates between brilliance and inconsistency -- even in the same game. In the first half against Ohio State, Manning connected on only 7 of 14 passes for 44 yards. Against Texas A&M last season, he was 5-of-15 for 28 yards. Oklahoma is probably not good enough to take advantage, but Manning needs to start faster for Texas to maintain its No. 1 ranking. Texas vs. Oklahoma prediction, picks It's always dangerous to bet on a big line in a major rivalry game, but it's getting harder than ever to trust Brent Venables' squad to come through. Three of Oklahoma's four games against Texas under Venables cleared a 17-point margin of victory, and this Sooners squad might be the worst one yet. College football sometimes surprises you, but... this would be a surprise. The defenses should control the game's outcome, as they both rank in the SEC's top five in points allowed. Texas will look to make it three straight wins over the Sooners, with the Sooners failing to score a touchdown in each of the last two games against the Longhorns. If Texas can bring home the Golden Hat again, it would be the first time since the turn of the century that the Longhorns won three straight games over the Sooners. ESPN's College GameDay was in Tuscaloosa on Saturday morning to preview the Georgia-Alabama game, but it spent much of its time on the Red River Rivalry. The crew of Desmond Howard, Rece Davis, Pat McAfee, Nick Saban, and celebrity guest picker Bryce Young all revealed their game picks for Texas-Oklahoma Here are the predictions: Oct 11, 2025; Dallas, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian takes a photo with players after the game against the Oklahoma Sooners at the Cotton Bowl. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Desmond Howard: Desmond Howard: The former Heisman winner and Michigan Wolverine is buying into the defenses with both of these teams. “Defensive struggle. We showed the statistics earlier,” Howard said. “Both quarterbacks are very similar statistically. I think that Texas will get it done.” It hasn’t been often that the former West Virginia Mountaineer has picked against the Longhorns recently, and that didn’t change here. That is despite Gameday doing a mid-show segment comparing the statistics of Arch Manning and John Mateer. “I've talked about Arch, and they're the number one team in the country for a reason,” McAfee said. “Say it with me, Tuscaloosa. Hook 'em.” Sep 10, 2022; Austin, Texas, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide quarterback Bryce Young (9) looks to throw a pass against the Texas Longhorns during the second half at at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports Pick: Texas The former Alabama quarterback who faced Texas once in his career, beating the Longhorns in a close 2022 game, didn’t pick against the Longhorns. Yeah, it's always a special atmosphere,” Young said. “ I'm sure it'll be fun, but yeah, I got Texas getting it done.” Steve Sarkisian’s former boss and mentor hasn’t been one prone to pick against his former assistant coaches. He is buying stock in the Longhorns to figure out the inconsistencies on offense. “I think Texas is playing really good defense,” Saban said. “I think Sark will get them fixed on offense. I think Texas gets it done.” Kirk Herbstreit The former Ohio State Buckeye completed the clean sweep of picks for the Longhorns. “Emotional game. Take the under here,” Herbstreit said. “It's gonna be a low-scoring game. These two defenses, I think, will play well. I agree. Texas wins.” Loading recommendations... picks.headline: Kirk Herbstreit Hesitatingly Picks Winner for Texas-Oklahoma Week 6 College Football Game
picks.blurb: Kirk Herbstreit Hesitatingly Picks Winner for Texas-Oklahoma Week 6 College Football Game Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Given that Texas is the No. 1 team in the nation and Oklahoma has been one of the SEC's biggest disappointments, this season's verion of the Red River Rivalry isn't necessarily being considered one of the best games in college football this week. But don't tell that conclusion to ESPN's Kirk Herbstreit, who thinks the ingredients are in place for a battle in this season's matchup. Herbstreit's Red River Pick While Texas is a solid road favorite against 2-2 Oklahoma, Herbstreit was thoughtful and reluctant to enter his decision on this game... before ultimately picking the Longhorns. Herbstreit certainly doesn't think the action goes down without a fight. "I think OU's going to make this game competitive," said Herbstreit on ESPN's College GameDay . "Because it's a rivalry game and you expect one team to win, that's always a dangerous receipe to me." Texas's Struggles QB Arch Manning could struggle, per Kirk Herbstreit, if Oklahoma can put him in long-yardage situations. (Randy Sartin-Imagn Images) | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Texas is the obvious favorite, but with two wins over ranked teams by a combined four points, the Longhorns haven't been a juggernaut, particularly on offense. QB Arch Manning has been underwhelming, currently sitting 10th of 16 qualifying SEC quarterbacks in QB rating. Manning's 7.5 yards per pass attempt ranks 11th of the passers. Manning is 14th in the league in passing yardage and his 7 touchdown passes ties for 11th. That said, Texas's offensive concerns still are minor compared to the issues at Oklahoma. Texas is the obvious favorite, but with two wins over ranked teams by a combined four points, the Longhorns haven't been a juggernaut, particularly on offense. QB Arch Manning has been underwhelming, currently sitting 10th of 16 qualifying SEC quarterbacks in QB rating. Manning's 7.5 yards per pass attempt ranks 11th of the passers. Manning is 14th in the league in passing yardage and his 7 touchdown passes ties for 11th. That said, Texas's offensive concerns still are minor compared to the issues at Oklahoma. Herbstreit Loves Oklahoma Defense Oklahoma is next to last in the SEC in scoring offense (22 points per game) and is dead last in total offense (321.3 yards per game). That's 57 yards per game behind 12th place Texas, and QB John Mateer has looked particularly lost with four interceptions on the young season and a performance so ugly against New Mexico that he admitted that he had to hear the crowd to clue him in on an open receiver on one play. While Oklahoma's offense has been woeful, Herbstreit notes, "Their defense has been playing at a championship level." Considering the occasional lapses in concentration from the Texas offense, Hebrstreit saw that as an advantage. "If they can get Arch [Manning] to 3rd and five, 3rd and seven, they can create havoc on him. They're one of the best third-down defenses in the country." Indeed, Oklahoma leads the SEC and currently ranks third nationally in allowing opponents to connect on just 23.1% of third downs (12 for 52). The Sooners are second in the conference in total defense, surrendering just 238 yards per game. The Final Pick Herbstreit seemed to give genuine thought to picking the Sooners for the upset. "I think this is a close game," he said. "I think OU's defense can keep them within striking distance. I just don't think they can win, with the offense the way they are playing." picks.headline: Paul Finebaum Predicts Texas-Oklahoma Winner in Eye-Catching Fashion
picks.blurb: Paul Finebaum Predicts Texas-Oklahoma Winner in Eye-Catching Fashion Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Paul Finebaum is many things, but not above a little casual trolling is certainly one of them. Known as one of the preeminent voices of SEC media well before his time began with ESPN, the network leans heavily on Finebaum's SEC expertise. And with the relatively recent expansion of the SEC, plenty of fan bases are getting to know Finebaum more and more. Add Oklahoma and Texas to that group, as the two former Big 12 stalwarts are getting to see more and more of Finebaum. This week on SEC Nation , Finebaum weighed in on the 2026 edition of the Red River Rivalry in his typical fashion. The four SEC Nation cast members weighed in on the Oklahoma/Texas game. Despite the show being in Norman, Oklahoma this week, the first three cast members went with the conventional wisdom and picked the Texas Longhorns who are favored by around a touchdown in the rivalry battle with the Sooners. Finebaum made it more interesting. Finebaum's Take "I keep hearing that you have a rivalry game and anything can happen. And you Sooners know that, right?" asked Finebaum. Having stoked the crowd, he then turned heel and disappointed them. "But I don't think you really have to factor that in because there's one team over here going up," continued Finebaum. "There's another team going down. And the Sooners are going down. Hook 'em, Horns!" THE PICKS ARE IN‼️ The SEC Nation crew make their picks for the Red River Rivalry 🤠 pic.twitter.com/8PCoNgnNNh Oklahoma's Troubles Finebaum delivered the unanimous vote for Texas and it's unsurprising as the top-ranked Longhorns travel to a 2-2 Oklahoma team that has had massive problems on offense this season. Since a 51-0 win over UTEP in Week 1, Oklahoma has scored just 10, 14, and 13 points in the past three games, which included a loss to Michigan and a 41-13 loss to Georgia. The Sooners failed to gain 300 yards in any of those three games. An 8-0 ESPN pick for Texas While Texas's offense has been somewhat inconsistent, the Longhorn defense has had enough strength to hold off Ohio State and Tennessee-- albeit by a combined four-point margin. While Oklahoma has an even more stout defense, the conventional wisdom is that a balanced Texas team can probably score enough points to win. While pregame pickers on both SEC Nation and College GameDay took time to shout out the OU defense , a unanimous 8-0 verdict between the two shows had the Longhorns winning. That said, few seemed to have as much fun in stoking the crowd as did Finebaum. Loading recommendations... My Texas vs. Oklahoma prediction and Week 6 college football picks expect Steve Sarkisian's defense to shut down the Sooners yet again today, Saturday, Oct. 10. For the full slate, see our Week 6 Top 25 predictions and best bets . TOP PICK Who will win Texas vs Oklahoma today? Pick: Texas -7.5 Recent Texas vs. Oklahoma rivalry history has been unkind to the Sooners, and I would take the Longhorns to cover as many as 9.5 points this year, as I did in my early Texas vs. Oklahoma prediction . Texas has beaten Oklahoma in three of Brent Venables' four Red River Rivalry games by an average of 32.3 points. In those three wins, the Longhorns held the Sooners to fewer than seven points, thanks to dominant defensive performances. This year's Texas defense might be the best one yet, ranking No. 3 in net adjusted EPA per play , No. 11 in success rate (36.5%), and No. 16 in havoc rate (20.6%). Oklahoma's offense could struggle to put up double digits against Texas. The Sooners are averaging 12.3 points per game in their last three games and rank last in the SEC in offensive success rate (39.2%), largely due to John Mateer's poor play. Last year against Texas, Mateer was as bad as it gets (three interceptions, six turnover-worthy plays, 34.6 QBR). Texas vs Oklahoma Over/Under pick: Under 39.5 Texas and Oklahoma are 6-2 to the Under combined and have hit it in three of the last four Red River Rivalry games. When the Sooners' offense doesn't score, the Under tends to hit at the Cotton Bowl, and this year's OU offense doesn't score (I like the Under down to 37.5 ). Oklahoma put up just 258 yards on Texas last year, and the Longhorns' defense is better this time around. It's ranked No. 5 by SP+ and has allowed more than 17 points once. That was to Ohio State and Heisman Trophy odds favorite Jeremiah Smith, and it allowed just three points in the second half to the Buckeyes. However, it's not just Oklahoma's offense that has struggled. Texas is averaging 22 ppg against Power Four opponents, and Oklahoma's defense is still feisty. The Sooners are 12th in the country in havoc rate (21.6%) , and Arch Manning has just one TD pass vs. two interceptions in P4 games. Texas vs Oklahoma combo The Red River Rivalry has been uncompetitive in three of Venables' four seasons in Norman. Oklahoma has a massive offensive problem, and there's no reason to believe this year will be any different. See more in our favorite college football combos for Week 6 . Mateer ranks 69th nationally in QBR (56.7) and has posted a 58.9 QBR or worse in three straight matchups, leading the Sooners to fewer than 300 total yards in each. OU's offense likely won't have its left tackle and is down one of its top receivers ( Trell Harris ) against a Texas defense that's allowing just 271 yards per game. However, the Sooners should slow Texas' offense down too. I have Texas winning Red River 24-13. First half total Under 19.5 Texas vs Oklahoma prop: Oklahoma team total Under 15.5 Oklahoma failed to score more than 13 points against Michigan , New Mexico , and Georgia . Those three defenses are ranked top 25 by SP+, as is Texas', which is allowing just 13.2 ppg. The Under on the Sooners' team total is worth playing at 14.5 or better . OU is averaging 3.0 ppg in its three Red River Rivalry losses under Venables, and I don't see the Sooners scoring more than 14 this year. The Longhorns' pass rush is one of the best in college football, with Colin Simmons ranking top 10 in the Power Four in pressures (18) and second nationally in sacks (7.5). Blocking him could be a massive problem for an Oklahoma offense expected to be without left tackle Michael Fasusi. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning. My Texas vs. Oklahoma prop picks attack three Unders in a Red River Rivalry showdown primed for a defensive battle. Although the Longhorns are favored by more than a touchdown for Saturday's 3:30 p.m. ET kickoff at the Cotton Bowl, points could come at a premium in our Texas vs. Oklahoma predictions . Find out more in my latest college football picks for Oct. 10. Best Texas vs Oklahoma props Prop pick #1: Arch Manning Under 210.5 passing yards Arch Manning's passing Under is playable down to 207.5 yards because he's topped 202 passing yards only once this season, and that came against Group of Six opponent Texas State. This is also the Texas quarterback's toughest passing matchup yet. Oklahoma ranks in the 95th percentile in passing-defense success rate , per GameOnPaper.com , and no opponent has thrown for more than 177 yards against the Sooners. Oklahoma has consistently forced offenses to work underneath and earn yards rather than giving up easy explosive plays. Manning threw for only 166 yards against the Sooners last year despite completing 77.8% of his passes. Virtually all of his passing numbers also declined on the road last season . Prop pick #2: Lloyd Avant Under 24.5 rushing yards Texas has a strength-on-weakness edge over Oklahoma in the rushing department . The Longhorns rank 14th nationally in yards per rush allowed , while the Sooners sit 123rd in yards per rush on offense. That mismatch isn't new, either, as Oklahoma managed just 48 rushing yards on 30 carries against Texas last season. The personnel situation makes things even tougher. Sooners running back Lloyd Avant is averaging just 3.8 yards per carry , while Oklahoma is dealing with injuries along the left side of its offensive line . Starting tackle Michael Fasusi is doubtful, while guard Eddy Pierre-Louis is questionable. If Oklahoma can't establish the run, Texas can force the Sooners into predictable passing situations, which will lead to fewer carries for Avant. Prop pick #3: Elijah Thomas Under 16.5 receiving yards According to Pro Football Focus , Sooners sophomore wideout Elijah Thomas ranks 964th among 996 qualified receivers , and I'd play this Under d own to 15.5 . Thomas was a four-star recruit coming out of high school, but he has mostly earned offensive opportunities because of his special-teams prowess. In fact, Thomas has more career tackles (10) than catches (five) . The matchup doesn't help, either. Texas ranks in the 96th percentile nationally in passing yards allowed per dropback , according to GameOnPaper . Even if Thomas sees a few extra routes, asking him to clear this number against an elite secondary is a tall order. away.headline: Longhorns Injury Report: RB Hollywood Smothers ready for Red River
away.blurb: Smothers was listed as questionable two weeks ago for Texas' trip to Knoxville to face Tennessee. The NC State transfer dressed, but was not used in the game. Sarkisian said was glad he didn't have to go to the Longhorns leading rusher and let him rest through the bye week for OU. “He was an emergency for us Saturday," Sark said after the 20-17 win over the Vols. "I felt like he probably could have gone, but what Raleek [Brown] had done in practice and Derek [Cooper] getting himself back, if I could have gotten out of that game with him not re-injuring himself, I think it would behoove us for the remainder of the season, and so we were able to do that. I think he’ll be fine in a couple weeks when we play OU." Defensive end Justus Terry and wide receiver Kaliq Lockett are both listed as doubtful for the OU game. Offensive lineman Jordan Coleman is out for Red River. Tight end Nick Townsend is probable. Adding Smothers back into the running back mix will be a big boost for a Texas offense that has yet to fire on all calendars this season. OU's defense will be one of the best UT faces this year. The Sooners injury list is lengthy with a total of 13 players listed. away.headline: 5 things for Texas football fans to know about the Oklahoma Sooners
away.blurb: On Saturday, the Texas football team will return from its bye week to face Oklahoma. And as it has for nearly a century, the Red River Rivalry game will be held at the Cotton Bowl in Dallas. While Oklahoma (2-2, 0-1 SEC) is unranked after beating UTEP and New Mexico but losing to both Michigan and Georgia, Texas (4-0, 1-0) is ranked No. 1 in the Associated Press top 25 poll. This marks the 14th time that either the Longhorns or Sooners were ranked No. 1 at the time of one of college football's top rivalry games. In the previous 13 instances, the No. 1-ranked team is 11-2 in the Red River Rivalry: • 1946: No. 1 Texas 20, Oklahoma 13 • 1954: No. 1 Oklahoma 14, No. 15 Texas 7 • 1956: No. 1 Oklahoma 45, Texas 0 • 1957: No. 1 Oklahoma 21, Texas 7 • 1963: No. 2 Texas 28, No. 1 Oklahoma 7 • 1964: No. 1 Texas 28, Oklahoma 7 • 1965: No. 1 Texas 19, Oklahoma 0 • 1978: No. 1 Oklahoma 31, No. 6 Texas 10 • 1984: No. 1 Texas 15, No. 3 Oklahoma 15 • 1987: No. 1 Oklahoma 44, Texas 9 • 2003: No. 1 Oklahoma 65, No. 11 Texas 13 • 2008: No. 5 Texas 45, No. 1 Oklahoma 35 • 2024: No. 1 Texas 34, No. 18 Oklahoma 3 Here are five things to know about the Sooners: 1. Oklahoma QB John Mateer is embattled After entering this season as a fringe Heisman Trophy candidate , John Mateer's star has faded. The fifth-year quarterback has thrown for 883 yards, eight touchdowns and four interceptions. Oklahoma even considered benching him during the second half of a 41-13 loss to Georgia on Sept. 26. A Texas native who spent the first three years of his college career at Washington State, Mateer will get his second shot at Texas after his unsuccessful comeback from a hand injury in last year's 23-6 loss. 2. Oklahoma hasn't scored a TD against Texas since 2023 Oklahoma has failed to score a touchdown in its last two games against Texas, which is something the Sooners haven't experienced against the Longhorns since 1909-10. Will the fact that this year's OU team is averaging 22 points per game make a difference? Maybe not. Oklahoma arrived at the Cotton Bowl in 2024 and 2025 averaging 28.6 and 33.8 points. 3. Ex-Texas WR Parker Livingstone hasn't caught on Of course, a big storyline in Dallas will be how Parker Livingstone fares against the Texas secondary. Livingstone played at Texas from 2024-25 and made two big third-down catches against the Sooners last year . But in the midst of UT's offseason roster makeover, Livingstone left for Oklahoma . With six catches through four games this season, he has not had a huge impact for a Sooners receiving corps led by Austin native Isaiah Sategna III. 4. Sooners defense is led by a veteran linebacker After becoming a starter during the second half of the 2025 season, Owen Heinecke has developed into a name worth knowing on the Oklahoma defense. The 6-foot-1, 230-pound linebacker is leading the Sooners with his 27 tackles, and Heinecke has also recorded a sack and a quarterback hurry. away.headline: Initial injury report released for No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma
away.blurb: For Texas, senior running back Hollywood Smothers remains off the injury report after sitting out against Tennessee with a lower-leg injury. Head coach Steve Sarkisian described the NC State transfer as an emergency option during that game. Still on the injury report after reportedly practicing last week is sophomore tight end Nick Townsend, who hasn’t played since suffering a bone bruise in his knee against Ohio State, but is now listed as probable. Less promising is the news with sophomore defensive lineman Justus Terry. The Georgia product sustained a toe injury warming up before the win over the Buckeyes, hasn’t played since, and is listed as doubtful along with sophomore wide receiver Kaliq Lockett, a new addition to the injury report. Remaining out is sophomore offensive lineman Jordan Coleman, who also missed the win over Tennessee in Knoxville. Oklahoma is a different story with four players listed as out, including transfer wide receiver Trell Harris, three players listed as doubtful, including left tackle Michael Fasusi, out since Week 1, five players listed as questionable, including guard Eddy Pierre-Louis, and one player listed as probable, linebacker Owen Heinecke. The sophomore tight end will be available for the Red River Rivalry.
