home.blurb: Another UCF Knights Offensive Lineman Out Against No. 18 Oklahoma State: Injury Report Breakdown Skip to main content SI.COM Jacob Maiava and Owen Spell were already ruled out by Wednesday night. Spell, who Frost said "wasn't 100%" after the Georgia State game due to plantar fasciitis, is set to miss a third consecutive game after getting ruled out on Wednesday. Meanwhile, his injury led to Maiava taking over as the Knights' new starting center, but now he is out for Saturday as well thanks to what Frost said was a soft tissue injury in his groin, though it was initially assumed to be a hip injury following the UCF's loss to Houston. Following Maiava's injury during the Houston game, Cooper Terpstra , listed as the Knights' backup right guard, took over at center, but was replaced later by Connor Meadows . With both Spell and Maiava out, whichever one of these two players does get the start at center is likely going to take up the right guard spot. Further down the depth chart, the offensive line could also be without backup right tackle Tyler Gibson , who was designated as questionable on Wednesday. Should he be ruled out as well, Laparka Langston and Justin Royes would likely become the players next in line for snaps on Saturday in place of the starting five linemen. THURSDAY UPDATE: Gibson was officially ruled out for Saturday's game in Thursday's player availability report. Lewis Carter has been ruled out , set to miss a third straight game after sustaining a lower-body injury during the Georgia State game. Jayden Jennings , who took over as a starter following Carter's injury, was designated as questionable following an injury sustained last weekend against Houston. Jahleel Culbreath , Carter's listed backup, was designated as probable . Given Culbreath is more likely to take the field in Stillwater on Saturday, he is the most likely option to get a starting role alongside Tackett Curtis should Jennings be ruled out. However, it could also present an opportunity for Rashad Henry and Phil Picciotti to earn some snaps as well. Cole Kozlowski , who received eligibility for this season thanks to a preliminary injunction by an Orange County judge, is also available. For the first time this season, Duane Thomas Jr. has not been ruled out in a Wednesday report, instead being designated as questionable . This opens the door for him to make his 2026 debut on Saturday, consistent with Frost's remarks on Monday that said Thomas had a chance to return in Stillwater. FRIDAY UPDATE: Thomas Jr. has been downgraded to doubtful for Saturday's game in Friday's player availability report. However, even if Thomas did return, the Knights' receivers would not be all hands on deck, as Caleb Rollerson was ruled out on Wednesday. The redshirt sophomore is a reserve option for the Knights and has caught four receptions for 38 yards and a touchdown so far this season. picks.blurb: Greg McElroy Picks UCLA vs. Oregon Winner With Dante Moore's Status Unclear Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN analyst Greg McElroy picked Oregon to beat unbeaten No. 21 UCLA on Saturday at Autzen Stadium, betting that the Ducks' run defense can contain first-year coach Bob Chesney's ground game whether Dante Moore or Dylan Raiola starts at quarterback. McElroy took the Ducks 31-21 on his Always College Football podcast and built the pick around a red-zone trend for Oregon coach Dan Lanning. "Dan Lanning is 39-1 in his career when Oregon gets more red-zone trips than the opponent," McElroy said. Who starts at quarterback for Oregon? Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola throws a pass as the Oregon Ducks face the USC Trojans | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Moore suffered a concussion in Oregon's 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26, and he returned to practice Monday in a helmet and shoulder pads. Still, Lanning hasn't cleared the former UCLA quarterback, and the Big Ten's first injury report for the game is due Wednesday night. Moore suffered a concussion in Oregon's 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26, and he returned to practice Monday in a helmet and shoulder pads. Still, Lanning hasn't cleared the former UCLA quarterback, and the Big Ten's first injury report for the game is due Wednesday night. Raiola replaced Moore at the Coliseum and went 19 of 25 for 289 yards and two touchdowns. However, McElroy pointed to the Nebraska transfer's history against ranked teams. "If you look back at his time at Nebraska, he was 0-5 against ranked football teams," McElroy said. "Well, UCLA is ranked." A Raiola start would also come one week before Oregon faces Nebraska. Wayne Knight vs. Oregon run defense UCLA running back Wayne Knight (3) looks on after scoring a touchdown during the second half against San Diego State | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect UCLA is 4-0 and 2-0 in the Big Ten after a 54-3 win at Maryland on Sept. 26. Chesney became the first UCLA coach since Red Sanders in 1949 to open his tenure 4-0 . UCLA is 4-0 and 2-0 in the Big Ten after a 54-3 win at Maryland on Sept. 26. Chesney became the first UCLA coach since Red Sanders in 1949 to open his tenure 4-0 . Running back Wayne Knight, who followed Chesney from James Madison , has 445 yards and nine touchdowns on 49 carries against FBS opponents. McElroy noted the Bruins average 7 yards per carry, the best mark in the country. But Oregon has allowed just nine runs of 10 or more yards. The Bruins' passing game is the concern. Quarterback Nico Iamaleava has thrown four touchdown passes, which McElroy said ranks 118th nationally, and Chesney's teams struggle when they have to lean on the pass. "Bob Chesney is 20-1 as an FBS head coach when his team runs fewer than 30 pass plays," McElroy said. "He is 1-3 when they have to throw it 40 or more times." Why did McElroy pick Oregon? Oregon Ducks head coach Dan Lanning runs out to the field with players before a game against the Portland State Vikings | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect McElroy expects Oregon to load up against the run and force Iamaleava to beat a defense that holds opponents to a 54% completion rate. McElroy expects Oregon to load up against the run and force Iamaleava to beat a defense that holds opponents to a 54% completion rate. "Oregon will completely sell out against the run," McElroy said. "So once the Bruins are forced to throw the ball, that's when the matchup starts to tilt pretty hard in the direction of the Ducks," McElroy added. UCLA's best upset path runs through turnovers. The Bruins are plus-8 in turnover margin, tied for third nationally, while Oregon has given the ball away twice all season. UCLA also averages 10 penalties per game, which McElroy said ranks 137th out of 138 teams, and that number becomes harder to overcome in a road environment like Autzen. History favors the Ducks, too. Oregon has won the last five meetings, and McElroy noted UCLA's last win in Eugene came in 2004, when Lanning was a freshman linebacker at William Jewell. In 2022, the Bruins started the season 6-0 before going to Oregon, but that UCLA team was a bit of a mirage. No, this isn't at the 1998 level yet, when the team was 10-0 and deep in the national title hunt before losing in a historic 49-45 thriller against Edgerrin James and Miami. And no, this UCLA team isn't there yet in Bob Chesney's first season, but if it pulls this off, everything changes. Oregon got back to being Oregon again with a 41-27 win over USC, but Dante Moore is out, Dylan Raiola is in, and this is when it has to flex at home and show just how much the Week 2 loss to Oklahoma State was a blip. UCLA vs Oregon: Quick Hits Oregon gets three home games in the next four weeks. It plays unbeaten UCLA this week, hosts currently unbeaten Nebraska next week, goes to Illinois, and then hosts Northwestern before traveling to Ohio State. UCLA plays three home games in a row after this, hosting Wisconsin, Michigan State, and Nevada before going to Minnesota. Oregon has won five straight in the series since 2017, last winning 34-13 in 2024. The one time it had a problem with a ground attack was against Oklahoma State, when it got hammered for 237 yards and close to six yards per carry. UCLA is fourth in the nation in rushing, averaging 281.5 yards per game and seven yards per carry. Oregon's run defense has had time to prepare – the loss to the Cowboys really was an aberration – but the Bruins get physical and grind teams down. UCLA has a pass rush and should be able to get to Raiola a bit against an Oregon offensive line that hasn't been a rock so far, but the passing game will blow up. UCLA vs Oregon Prediction, Betting Lines The key to UCLA is the ability to hang around and then take over in the second half. The problem is that it won't be able to do that so easily against an Oregon defense that's No. 1 in the nation in third down stops. The Bruins are going to be a problem for the Big Ten the rest of the season – seriously, even with a loss here, they still have a great shot to be in the CFP mix – but Oregon really is one of the ten best teams in college football, and when it has to midway through the second half, it'll show why. Now, after a much-needed bye week, Oregon is ready to get back out there once again, facing their second straight top-25 matchup. The No. 21 UCLA Bruins are coming to town with a 4-0 record and a hot streak that has captured the attention of the college football world. Will the Ducks be able to stop that in its tracks, or will Bob Chesney's team keep on rolling and prove against Oregon that it belongs among the contenders in the Big Ten? All week, we've broken down the game and analyzed what we expect to happen, but now let's take a look at what the national media guys think. Here's a look at what some of the biggest names in the sport are saying about Oregon's matchup against UCLA on Saturday afternoon: Pick: Oregon 45, UCLA 32 Analysis: "I expect a lot of points in this one, but Oregon gets it done. I think Oregon wins this one, 45-32, and Oregon covers the 11.5. Don't feel great about that cover right there, but I do think Oregon gets it done." Pick: Oregon -11.5 Analysis: "I feel like this is going to be a competitive game in the first half, maybe even competitive in the second half, and then the fourth quarter is Oregon's, and they ended up covering that 11.5." Analysis: "I love Oregon -11.5 here. I think they found out who they are. I think they're beginning to see that snowball effect that's taken place where they start to make the climb into the playoffs." Dan Rubenstein Pick: Oregon 38, UCLA 21 Analysis: "I think the talent will win out. I think the explosion will win out, and I have Oregon winning this game, something like 38-21." Ty Hildenbrandt Pick: Oregon 34, UCLA 24 Analysis: "The only way it works for UCLA is if they are running efficiently enough, though. If they are running efficiently enough, like you said, early downs, finding a way to create some of those passing lanes on their own terms. I think the Oregon pass rush is good enough to dictate their terms, and I think I don't think Oregon is going to fall victim to it for the entirety of the game." Pick: Oregon 34, UCLA 23 Analysis: "I think UCLA is in a really good spot with Bob Chesney, but I think Oregon wins, and I think Oregon covers. Final score in Autzen: Ducks 34, Bruins 23." Greg McCelroy Pick: UCLA +11.5, Oregon win Analysis: "I think UCLA can run the ball with anybody. They're excellent. I just don't know if they're going to be able to run the ball all over Oregon because this is a huge step up in competition, and Oregon will completely sell out against the run. I'll take the Ducks, but by 10, there in Autzen Stadium. The last time that LSU played in Lexington, it didn't go very well for the Tigers. LSU lost 41-21 on the road to Kentucky in 2021. It was the second straight SEC loss for the Tigers under then head coach Ed Orgeron. It was a loss that all but sealed the fate of Orgeron (especially after he admitted that LSU's defensive line got out-physicaled). The Tigers will return to Lexington this weekend for a matchup against the Wildcats. And while no players remain on the roster from the 2021 LSU team, I'm sure head coach Lane Kiffin will use the loss to Kentucky in 2021 as motivation. ESPN's Cole Cubelic shares how he thinks the LSU vs Kentucky game will play out ESPN's Cole Cubelic shared some thoughts this week on the LSU vs Kentucky matchup. Cubelic noted that he likes the momentum that Kentucky has right now, but he doesn't think the Wildcats can consistently pressure Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt. "I like this game being at Kroger Field," said Cubelic . "I like the momentum Kentucky has right now. The problem is that Kentucky can't get to the quarterback, and I think Sam Leavitt has gotten better in the pocket — he was forced to (get better in the pocket) with the hamstring two weeks ago against Texas A&M. And he did it again last week. "[Leavitt] being able to find success from the pocket and Kentucky not being able to get home, that's going to be a problem. And LSU is going to score. So I think LSU gets the win. I'm not going to touch the 8.5 (points) there that LSU is favored by, but I may like the over 51.5 in this game." LSU and Kentucky will kick off at 6:00 PM CT/7:00 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ESPN. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. LSU will enter this SEC road matchup against Kentucky at 4-1 after cruising past McNeese 63-14 on Saturday night. The Tigers have now won two straight since their loss at Ole Miss, including an impressive 35-6 victory over Texas A&M. Kentucky also comes into this matchup at 4-1 after escaping South Carolina with a 35-34 overtime victory Saturday. The Wildcats have now won three straight since suffering their only loss of the season, a 45-17 defeat against Alabama. For LSU, the game represents an opportunity to build on the momentum of the past two weeks while picking up a much-needed SEC road victory. The Tigers have looked like a much more complete team since their loss at Ole Miss, particularly on defense, and will now have to carry that success away from Tiger Stadium. The Wildcats have already shown they can be dangerous in the SEC after going into College Station and defeating Texas A&M 31-21 before surviving an overtime battle at South Carolina. Now they will return home looking to add another victory to their record against LSU. Saturday will also mark LSU's first trip to Lexington since 2021, when Kentucky defeated the Tigers 42-21. LSU hasn't won at Kentucky since the memorable 33-30 "Bluegrass Miracle" in 2002, adding another storyline to the Tigers season. Here's my North Dakota State vs. UNLV prediction and college football pick for Saturday, October 10. North Dakota State vs. UNLV Pick: North Dakota State Team Total Under 25.5 My UNLV vs. North Dakota State best bet is on the Rebels' total points. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page and make sure to download our Action Network app to get the latest picks and betting analysis. North Dakota State vs UNLV Odds North Dakota State vs UNLV point spread : North Dakota State -3.5 (-102), UNLV +3.5 (-120) North Dakota State vs UNLV over/under : 48.5 (-105o / -115u) North Dakota State vs UNLV moneyline : North Dakota State -160, UNLV +130 North Dakota State has been impressive this season in its first at the FBS level, and the transition has gone as well as anyone would have predicted. The Bison are 5-0 both straight up and against the spread, led by their defense, which is tied with Miami for first in the country. NDSU has allowed just 9.8 points per game this season. The Bison have remained true to the identity that brought them so much success at the FCS level, using a ball-control offense, power running game and rock-solid defense to win games. The offense isn't as explosive, dominant or dynamic as in previous seasons, but quarterback Nathan Hayes has completed 65% of his passes with 995 yards through the air and a 7:2 touchdown-to-interception ratio. The ground game has been effective and efficient without being overly explosive. NDSU is averaging 171 rushing yards per game as a team on 4.2 yards per carry. DJ Scott and Myles Mitchell garner the majority of the carries and have rushed for 512 yards between the pair with seven combined rushing scores. Jackson Williams is the most consistent receiver and has hauled in 22 passes for 358 yards this season. He'll see a decent amount of the target share in this game. The defense has been unbelievably impressive while holding four of its five opponents to 10 points or less. The Bison have been strong against the run and have held their opponents — including Air Force — to just three yards per carry and 102 yards per game on the ground. The secondary hasn't surrendered explosive plays, and only 40% of opponent red-zone trips have resulted in touchdowns. This bunch will have its hands full against UNLV on the road this week, but I expect a decent showing out of this defense. UNLV has to consider this season mildly disappointing thus far, as the Rebels dropped the season opener at home against Memphis and were embarrassed on the road at North Texas earlier in the season. Recently, however, the offense has come to life with back-to-back games, scoring 38 and 39 points in wins over Akron and Cal . The Rebels have their sights set on continuing to remain in contention for a Mountain West title. The offense is going to remain run-oriented, as Jai'Den Thomas leads the way with 383 yards and a pair of rushing scores. Thomas provides explosiveness and versatility out of the running back position and is a great complement to quarterback Jackson Arnold , who has run for 270 yards while leading the team with five rushing scores. Arnold has thrown the ball well over the last two weeks, and connecting on the downfield passes has spring-loaded the scoring for UNLV. While only 59% of his passes have been completed, Arnold creates well on the move, has thrown eight touchdown passes without an interception, and many of his incomplete passes were throwaways to avoid sacks. The eyesore has been the offensive line, which has surrendered 14 sacks and 28 tackles for loss. This group will have its work cut out for them against a strong Bison defensive front. The UNLV defense isn't a strong unit, but it has played well at times this season. Holding Hawaii to six points on the road was quite a feat, and Akron was held scoreless after halftime a couple of weeks back. Cal scored 31 points last week against this defense in completely fluky fashion. One scoring drive was a 91-yard touchdown pass where a defender fell, and another missed a tackle. After halftime, UNLV surrendered a scoring drive of 52 yards, followed up by fumbling the ensuing kickoff. The offense has run a slower tempo recently and will likely do so here to keep the defense fresh, but this stop unit will have to be rock-solid in order to see UNLV compete with NDSU. This game has North Dakota State listed as a 3.5-point road favorite with a total set at 48.5. This total has been bet down from 51.5 on the opener. I agree with the move and feel this matchup is one between even teams. I'm willing to take NDSU's team total under 25.5. This game will be played at a very slow pace, and the Bison will operate very slowly when they have the ball. While this offense has put up a decent amount of points this season, the strength of schedule disparity in this matchup is monumental. North Dakota State has feasted on weak defenses, including Sac State , Fordham and Air Force . The Rebs have controlled the line of scrimmage this season and have done well to prevent explosives on the ground. NDSU won't find the chunk plays on the ground in this game, and I wouldn't be surprised to see UNLV get the Bison off the field early in this game until they settle in. The Rebels have given up some explosiveness through the air, something NDSU is ill-equipped to exploit in this matchup. UNLV has an excellent red-zone defense that has allowed just eight touchdowns on 17 attempts. I look for the UNLV stop unit to bow up in the red area and force NDSU to settle for field goals, something we've seen in recent weeks. The Rebels will run the ball a decent amount, and while they'll be effective, they won't be explosive. NDSU has made a concerted effort defensively to keep everything in front of it, and the defense forces long, methodical drives. UNLV's performance in the red zone has been terrible this season, as only 53% of trips have resulted in touchdowns, and the Rebs gamble on fourth-and-goal a lot. Doing that again will leave NDSU with long fields, so the Bison will take time off the clock on long, methodical drives. I think this game will be a lower-scoring competitive grind, with the winning team not surpassing 24 total points. This is a tough trip against a team that has played a much tougher schedule to date, so I will bet that the Bison offense struggles for the first time this season. Pick: North Dakota State Team Total Under 25.5

picks.headline: Bold Predictions for Georgia-Alabama Showdown
picks.blurb: Bold Predictions for Georgia-Alabama Showdown Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Alabama Crimson Tide and the Georgia Bulldogs will face off on Saturday and are going to have to weather both the storm of each other and Hurricane Isaias. As always, this matchup brings memorable moments. It brings drama. It brings instant-classics. I have to find a way to get bold with it. I lost out on all three of my bold predictions for the Vanderbilt game after hitting on one against Oklahoma. Fortunately, I have seen this movie plenty of times. Here are three bold takes for the game between Kirby Smart’s Dawgs and Kalen DeBoer’s Crimson Tide that I think can legitimately happen. 5 Total Turnovers Between Both Teams The ground will be wet, the wind will be hard and the rain will be coming down. The weather is projected to calm down for actual gametime, but now tabbed as Hurricane Isaias is going to make its mark all the way up the state of Alabama. You know what that means: sloppy football. We already saw the Georgia Bulldogs struggle with fumbles during the rainy Western Kentucky game in the second week. I suspect that could be an issue again if the weather truly is complicated. Alabama’s quarterback Keelon Russell, as good as he is, has not faced a defensive unit as talented or as violent as Georgia’s. He has been pretty clean this year, throwing only two interceptions and losing only one fumble to this point, but I predict he turns the ball over at least once himself. I would probably predict that even without the weather. Turnovers happen when these two teams face off. The weather will induce more of them. I am predicting five will come true. Gunner Stockton Scores Two Touchdowns on the Ground Georgia’s redshirt senior quarterback has yet to score a touchdown with his legs this season – something he did 10 times in 2025, leading the Dawgs in that category. I think he will do it twice on Saturday night. Stockton has not carried the ball near as much this season as he did at this point a year ago. He exploded for almost 100 yards on the ground at Arkansas thanks to a career-long 62-yard run. Georgia also hasn’t played in a big game yet. Stockton’s legs were a favorite in their important matchups a season ago. The danger comes in the red zone for opposing defenses. He had a red zone rushing touchdown against Tennessee. He ran two in against Kentucky. He scored the dagger with his legs against both Texas and Auburn. He ran one in from 22 yards out against Ole Miss in the regular season and then ran for two scores against the Rebels in the Sugar Bowl. I think Stockton will find the end zone again, and I think it will happen twice. It is the piece of Georgia’s red zone offense - which is extremely multiple - that hasn’t been dished out yet this season. Nate Frazier has his first 100-Yard Game of the Season Especially because of the potentially awful weather, I think Georgia is going to run the football a ton. Nate Frazier has gotten his rest since getting dinged up against Arkansas. He was off to a super hot start that has been slowed down due to him virtually missing 2.5 games. Chauncey Bowens has been ruled out for this game due to a foot injury he suffered last weekend. Even with the emergence and explosiveness of Dwight Phillips Jr., Frazier will likely see the bulk of the touches out of the backfield. Georgia operates a committee-style running back room, and Smart keeps saying that Georgia will continue to spread the football around. Frazier is still the lead back, and he will have his touches increased in big games. Loading recommendations... The analysts on College GameDay closed the three-hour morning show from Coleman Coliseum by picking the winner of this top-10 SEC showdown. Former Alabama head coach Nick Saban is one of the analysts, alongside Desmond Howard, Pat McAfee, Kirk Herbstreit and host Rece Davis. They are also joined by a celebrity guest each week, with Saturday's being former Alabama and current Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young . So, which panelists picked Alabama over Georgia, and how many chose the Bulldogs over the Crimson Tide? Note: Davis, the host, doesn't make picks, and the same is said for Herbstreit, who is on the call tonight. Desmond Howard: Alabama Nick Saban: Alabama Bryce Young: Alabama Pat McAfee: Georgia Saban : "You know, I think Georgia's got one of the most complete teams in the country. I love Kirby, he's had a very consistent identity with his teams — tough, physical and all of that. But I really like the togetherness of Alabama's team this year, so I'm going Roll Tide, baby." Young : "Seeing how well a team plays together here at Bama, watching the togetherness, the secondary gelling with all of the turnovers they're creating, and I think the X-factor is Keelon Russell. Watching him develop, watching how well he's playing, watching him have command, I'm a huge fan, I think he's super special. So, of course, Roll Tide." Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer joined the College GameDay set for a segment earlier in the show and was asked if there's something that the college football world doesn't see that makes him believe in the Crimson Tide. UA started the season ranked No. 13 in the AP Top 25, but is now 5-0 and the No. 6 team in the renowned poll. "There’s a third field that we don’t practice as much on, but it’s where the grind happened in the offseason. And I think just the lessons learned and the things that we went through, the guys have this belief and trust because they know that everyone’s doing the work." Alabama's Practice Field 3 was a staple of the summer, and BamaCentral spoke with nine different Crimson Tide players about the haunting workouts that occurred there. Alabama leads the all-time series against Georgia 45-27-4, with the first matchup occurring on Nov. 2, 1895. The Crimson Tide has a 24-13-4 home record against the Bulldogs and has won eight of the past 10 overall meetings. However, Georgia has had the last laugh, beating the Crimson Tide 28-7 in the 2025 SEC Championship Game. Alabama finished with -3 rushing yards and was without multiple key players. It was just the second time that season, with the other being the previous Oklahoma matchup, that the Alabama defense did not force a turnover. It was the second time Alabama faced the Bulldogs in 2025, as the Crimson Tide won the first game 24-21 in Athens. Loading recommendations... Georgia is fresh off a smackdown on Vanderbilt, 38-14, while Alabama dismantled Mississippi State 56-23. This has game of the year potential, and there's been a lot of them in the SEC already! Georgia has the No. 1 rated offense and defense per PFF, averages the most points in the country, and allow the third-fewest rushing yards per game (57.4) — and all of that will be put to the test against Alabama. The Bulldogs pitched a second-half shutout against Vanderbilt and won 38-14 after leading 21-14 at the half. Georgia has allowed 20 or fewer points in all five games and 44 points over the last three games against Arkansas, Oklahoma, and Vanderbilt. The offense put up 471 total yards of offense, doubled Vanderbilt's first downs (26-13), and held the Commodores to 85 rushing yards. Alabama is coming off arguably their most impressive performance of the season. The Tide destroyed Mississippi State, 56-23, never trailing in the game. Alabama outgained Mississippi State in yards 483-302, went 6-of-9 on third downs, and forced four turnovers (2 INT, 2 Fumbles). Keelon Russell had another dominant outing with 301 total yards and four touchdowns (3 pass, 1 rush). Russell is climbing the Heisman Trophy rankings and a win over Georgia would likely jolt him to the top spot. Alabama has owned the series against Georgia winning 10 of the past 12, but the Bulldogs won the previous matchup 28-7. Let's dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Game Details and How to Watch Georgia vs Alabama Date: Saturday, October 10, 2026 Time: 7:30 PM Eastern Site: Bryant-Denny Stadium City: Tuscaloosa, AL TV/Streaming: ABC Game Odds for Georgia vs Alabama The latest odds as of Tuesday courtesy of DraftKings : Moneyline: Georgia Bulldogs (+102), Alabama Crimson Tide (-122) Spread: Alabama -1.5 (-112) Total: 52.5 points #2 Georgia Bulldogs Head Coach: Kirby Smart 2026 Record: 5-0 (3-0) Offensive Points Per Game: 51.4 PPG (1st) Defensive Points Per Game: 13.4 (12th) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 97th 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 20th The Georgia Bulldogs Offense: Georgia is the highest scoring offense in the country which is odd because in years past, Kirby Smart has taken is foot off the gas against early season opponents. Georgia's scored 45, 41, and 38 points against SEC opponents so far with 471, 464, and 306 total yards of offense. Georgia ranks sixth in third-down offense (54.9%), fifth in passing efficiency (188.72), and 13th in turnover margin per game (+1.2). One area that will be of interest is Georgia's red zone offense is 51st in the country with a 25-of-28 conversion rate (89.3%), but the fourth-most red zone attempts. Georgia has to be aggressive in the red zone at Alabama. Field goals likely won't cut it. Georgia Player to Watch on Offense: QB Gunner Stockton In last year's SEC Championship Game, Gunner Stockton threw for three touchdowns on 20-of-26 for 156 yards. Georgia cruised 28-7. This matchup won't be as easy and could feature double the points. Stockton tossed three touchdowns versus Vanderbilt last week after combing for two touchdowns in the two weeks prior. Stockton hasn't been asked to do much this season due to all the talent around him, including the running back committee. Stockton has a 13:1 TD to INT ratio this season and a 75.7 completion percentage. The Georgia Bulldogs Defense: Georgia's allowing 244.6 yards per game (7th) and that will likely go up after this showdown. We know Georgia is great at getting pressure (PFF rank of 22 for pressure) or getting coverage sacks (PFF rank of 3 for coverage), but the two areas that will determine the game is third downs and red zone defense. Georgia's defense has a 33.8% third-down defense (44th) and have only allowed 11 red zone trips this season, but 10 of them have resulted in points (8 TDs, 2 FGs). Georgia Player to Watch on Defense: LB Chris Cole Chris Cole is a projected first round pick in the upcoming draft as a three-year player for Georgia. Cole opened the season with a half-sack, and added anther against Oklahoma with two fumble recoveries. Cole had 60 tackles last season, ranking fourth, and a team-leading 4.5 sacks. Cole has 22 tackles and 1.5 sacks to this season. Last year, Cole had five tackles versus Alabama and a sack. Alabama Player to Watch on Offense: QB Keelon Russell Keelon Russell now has a rushing touchdown in three-straight games and four out five, plus three or more passing touchdowns in three consecutive games. He is on fire and now the third in odds for the Heisman. Russell now has 11 passing touchdowns to two interceptions, 1,414 yards through the air, and 184 on the ground. Georgia hasn't won a game against Alabama in Tuscaloosa since 2007. The Bulldogs will be looking to end that streak this weekend when they play on the road against the Crimson Tide. Both teams enter the game with a 5-0 record. The winner will instantly be one of the favorites to be the top overall seed in the College Football Playoff later this year. ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Georgia vs Alabama ESPN's Greg McElroy, a former Crimson Tide quarterback, made his prediction for the game and he thinks the outcome will be decided by just three points. McElroy has Alabama leaving Bryant-Denny Stadium with a 31-28 win. "Alabama has 13 takeaways this year," said McElroy on Tuesday . "That's top two in the sport. (Georgia QB) Gunner Stockton has thrown one interception all season, so something's got to give here. If Alabama can steal one or maybe two possessions, then that gives them a significant edge in a game that is very much a toss-up. I'm taking the Crimson Tide 31, Georgia 28. "On paper, Georgia has the much better defense. They give up less than four yards per play. That's the best in college football. But right now, they haven't seen anything quite like what Alabama has offensively. (Alabama QB) Keelon Russell is playing the best football of anybody on the entire field, and Georgia's going to have to blitz, I think, to get home before he lets it go. Kirby Smart is 90-3 in his career when Georgia scores 30 or more, and we've got the Bulldogs stopping just short of that. He's also 2-7 against Alabama and 120-14 against everybody else. So it's going to be very hard to take the Bulldogs against a really improved Alabama football team in Tuscaloosa. "I also think Alabama will force a takeaway or two that will ultimately be the difference in what is a three-point game. Look, Georgia brings the better defense to Bryant-Denny on Saturday night, but I think Alabama has the edge in just about everything else. Give me the Tide, 31-28." Georgia and Alabama are set to kick off at 6:30 PM CT/7:30 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ABC. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. picks.blurb: College Football 27 sim predicts winner, score of Georgia vs. Alabama - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football winners/losers Oklahoma stuns Texas Marvin Harrison Jr. getting traded Valkyries finish sweep Angel Reese: Finals Barbie College Football 27 sim predicts winner, score of Georgia vs. Alabama Georgia Bulldogs running back Nate Frazier (3) runs against the Alabama Crimson Tide Owen Hillman, UGA Wire Fri, October 9, 2026 at 8:34 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Georgia Bulldogs (5-0, 3-0 in SEC) face their biggest test of the season against the Alabama Crimson Tide (5-0, 3-0 in SEC). Both teams have looked like national championship contenders; inclement weather concerns persist, and Kirby Smart's record against Alabama isn't very promising. Georgia has had strong wins against everyone they've faced, winning by at least 20 against every opponent (Tennessee State, Western Kentucky, Arkansas, Oklahoma, Vanderbilt). However, Alabama has played a tougher schedule, with Eastern Carolina and Florida State as their non-conference opponents so far, and has won against now-ranked Kentucky, South Carolina, and formerly ranked Mississippi State. There's a lot of pressure for the Bulldogs to keep rolling, and considering the state of the SEC, this could decide a contestant in the SEC championship too. Georgia vs. Alabama College Football 27 simulation Result This sim was conducted with the idea that Isiah Canion, Josh Ford, and Jorden Edmonds would be out. They were all listed as questionable on the injury report. Neither team got on the board in the first quarter due to the field conditions. It wasn't until the second quarter that the Crimson Tide struck first, with Daniel Hill rushing in a touchdown from 19 yards out to make it 7-0 at 9:44. Both teams exchanged punts, then on Georgia's next drive, Peyton Woodring nailed a 39-yard field goal to make it 7-3 at 2:50. Then, 40 seconds later, Keelon Russell's pass was intercepted by Justin Williams, who ran it back 19 yards for a touchdown to give Georgia a 10-7 halftime lead. Alabama countered with a Conor Talty 40-yard field goal at 8:33 to knot it up at 10, but then Georgia went on a long drive, capped off with a Nate Frazier touchdown to make it 17-10 with 3:22 left. Conor Talty kicked another field goal, this time from 37 yards out, to make it 17-13 by 8:13 in the fourth quarter, but Gunner Stockton fired a 73-yard bomb to Sacovie White-Helton for a touchdown to make it 24-13 Georgia. Nate Frazier essentially iced the game, as he ran in his second touchdown of the day from nine yards out to make it 31-13 by 3:33 in the fourth quarter. Alabama would get a garbage-time touchdown with Keelon Russell completing a screen pass to Kaleb Edwards to reach the final score of 31-20. Alabama got one more try, but Raylen Wilson picked off Keelon Russell again on the final play. It wasn't the most glamorous win for Georgia, but they got the job done. Both Georgia and Alabama had 4.5 yards per play, and Alabama did better on third down (eight for 16) than Georgia (five for 14). However, Georgia won the turnover battle, picking off Keelon Russell twice, while the running game did the rest. Gunner Stockton was uninspiring, going 17 for 25 for 161 yards and a touchdown and no interceptions. However, Nate Frazier came through on his return, with 95 yards and two touchdowns on 22 carries. The trenches helped Georgia win too. Georgia's offensive line did allow three sacks against Alabama, all by Jah-Marien Latham, but the Bulldog defensive line sacked Russell seven times, including three by Elijah Griffin and three by Josh Horton. Georgia would be 6-0 and in contention for the No. 1 seed if this were to hold in real life. Georgia would cover, considering they were 1.5-point underdogs against Alabama, and the under would hit by half a point. That would be an acceptable result for Georgia fans. The sim is 4-0 in predicting matchups, so hopefully this holds up too. This article originally appeared on UGA Wire: College Football 27 sim predicts winner, score of Georgia vs. Alabama

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 19 USC desperately needs a win to remain in the CFP hunt, while Penn State looks to avoid a 0-3 start in the Big Ten Imagn Images It's a must-win game for both teams , as No. 19 USC travels to take on Penn State on Saturday in Happy Valley. Penn State enters the game with its season seemingly spiraling out of control. After a 3-0 start in nonconference play under new coach Matt Campbell, the Nittany Lions have dropped their first two Big Ten games, and didn't look particularly inspiring in either. The offense struggled mightily in losses to Wisconsin and Northwestern , and last week, the defense was gashed by Northwestern's rushing attack. Suddenly, a schedule that was considered one of the easiest in the Big Ten before the season began looks far more difficult for the Nittany Lions. Not that things have been much easier for their opponents. The Trojans are 5-1 on the season and are coming off a win, but have looked shaky for three straight games. They found themselves in a shootout with Rutgers three weeks ago, followed that up with a 14-point home loss to Oregon , and last week flirted with disaster against a Washington team that hadn't looked impressive to start the season. Now they're on the road against a team with its back against the wall, and a second loss (with Ohio State and Indiana still to come) could crush USC's playoff chances. USC vs. Penn State: Need to know It's the White-Out game: Penn State's White-Out game is a newer tradition in college football , having begun in 2007, but it's quickly become one of the games Penn State fans look forward to most. Everybody in Beaver Stadium is dressed in white and screaming at their absolute loudest. Unfortunately, the results haven't always matched the intensity. Penn State is only 11-7 in White-Out games, but that's partly because the Nittany Lions reserve the tradition for their toughest games. It's a battle of the two winningest QBs in college football: That fact probably caught you by surprise, didn't it? Well, it's true. Penn State's Rocco Becht comes into this game with 29 wins as a starting QB in his college career. That's more than any other QB in the country. USC's Jayden Maiava is tied for second with 24. So Becht will either widen the gap this week, or Maiava will narrow it. Penn State hoping to avoid a 0-3 start in Big Ten again: Last season, the Nittany Lions started 0-6 in Big Ten play. It was an unexpected slide that led to James Franklin's mid-season firing. If they lose here, they'll be 0-3 in the Big Ten for the second straight season. The last time that happened was the 2003 and 2004 seasons. Of course, Matt Campbell could take some solace if his team loses. He'd be the first Penn State full-time head coach to start his tenure with a 3-3 mark since Joe Paterno in 1966. I don't like either side of the total, so I'm being asked to back a Penn State team that's looked terrible lately as a favorite, or take a USC team that's really struggled on the road under Lincoln Riley as a small dog. Frankly, there's no right option here, and I don't recommend taking any side. But, unlike you, I don't have a choice, so I guess I'm less terrified of USC +1.5 than anything else. Students walking around the campus heard lots of crowd noise coming from the Trojans practice field. That's because USC blared that energy through the loud speakers. Even true freshman edge rusher Luke Wafle admitted to being spooked by the sound. "It scared me the first time they were doing sound checks, and I was walking out of my class," Wafle told reporters on Oct. 8. Wafle sounds locked in on preparing for the noise levels, though, along with the rest of his Trojans teammates. This marked the first time USC practiced with noise this season. The Saturday, Oct. 10 matchup marks the seventh time the former Oklahoma coach, Riley, will face the ex-Iowa State leader, Campbell. But it'll be the first time they meet in the Big Ten. Riley owns the upper hand in the head-to-head matchups against Campbell's Cyclone teams, going 4-2 all-time against him and ISU. But Riley already knows what to expect from a Campbell-led team . "Going back to Iowa State, they've always used their tight ends really well, and they're doing so here [Penn State]. Defensively, they look a lot like the past Penn State teams in being big up front," Riley said during his Oct. 5 appearance on Trojans Live. "They've got really good athletes and talented players, and they're excellent on the back end. It's a well-coached football team, and it'll be a heck of a night." Oregon blocked out the noise and won in double overtime to prevent a Penn State home win. And the Ducks turned to a silent count on offense to withstand the noise. Perhaps USC rolls with something similar in this showdown. But Riley's past success against Campbell, plus USC showing signs of resurgence on defense, should be enough to avoid the upset. picks.headline: College GameDay makes picks for USC vs. Penn State whiteout
picks.blurb: The No. 19 USC Trojans enter Saturday night’s clash against the Penn State Nittany Lions at Beaver Stadium with their College Football Playoff hopes on the line. The Trojans will play in one of their most hostile environments this season: the Nittany Lions' annual whiteout game at Beaver Stadium, which is in primetime on NBC , with kickoff scheduled for 4:30 p.m. PT. The Trojans are currently the underdogs, despite the Nittany Lions suffering two straight losses to the Wisconsin Badgers and the Northwestern Wildcats. DraftKings Sportsbook lists the Trojans as 1.5-point underdogs against the Nittany Lions. That didn’t stop a majority of ESPN’s College GameDay crew from picking the Trojans to beat the Nittany Lions as a road underdog. Here’s a look at the GameDay crew’s picks. ESPN College GameDay Predictions Desmond Howard: USC Nick Saban: USC Pat McAfee: Penn State Bryce Young (guest picker): USC Kirk Herbstreit: USC Can USC Pull Off a Statement Road Win Over Penn State? Despite being underdogs and struggling on the road under coach Lincoln Riley, USC’s offense has been among the Big Ten's best this season. Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava, who is in his second season as USC’s full-time starter, enters Saturday night’s matchup against the Nittany Lions as the Big Ten’s leading passer with 1,744 yards, 15 touchdowns, and three interceptions. Two of those three interceptions came in the Trojans' last two games against the No. 13 Oregon Ducks and Washington Huskies, which could be a concern for USC’s offense against the Nittany Lions, as one turnover could be costly in a game like Saturday night’s with Penn State. The Trojans are also depleted at wide receiver, which has always been a strength of their offense under Riley. The latest season-ending injuries to Corey Simms and Terrell Anderson are crushing blows to the Trojans' offense that will affect them in Saturday night’s game against USC. A pair of freshmen, wide receiver Trent Mosley and tight end Mark Bowman, are also listed as questionable for the primetime matchup against the Nittany Lions. Their potential absence will be yet another crushing blow for the Trojans' offense. Facing such a hostile environment on Saturday night against the Nittany Lions, it’s crucial the Trojans start fast and avoid mistakes early on in the game. In their 25-21 home win over the Washington Huskies at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in Week 5, the Trojans offense got off to a slow start and even trailed by 11 early in the third quarter, before scoring 15 unanswered points to win. This is something the Trojans can’t afford to let happen on Saturday night when they face the Nittany Lions at Beaver Stadium. USC looks for its first win over Penn State as a member of the Big Ten, as the two last met in 2024 in Los Angeles, a game the Nittany Lions won 33-30 in overtime. Penn State hosts USC on Saturday night as the Trojans make their first visit to Beaver Stadium since 1994 and for the first time as a Big Ten opponent. The Trojans bring a dangerous offense to the game but are faced with some concerns about the defense. Can Penn State find its offense against the Trojans and pull off a big win against a ranked opponent in the whiteout game? Here are our final score and player of the game predictions for Penn State's Week 6 game against USC, along with some brief thoughts on the matchup. Kevin McGuire, Lead Writer The last couple of weeks have set off some serious alarms for me about Penn State, and that does not fill me with a great amount of confidence in the Nittany Lions going into this matchup against USC. The Trojans have struggled with the defense this season but I'm not seeing the firepower necessary to keep things too competitive with the Trojans on Saturdya night. After Northwestern ran all over Penn State's defense, I think the Trojans would be smart to try mimicking that with King Miller setting the tone on the ground and allowing Jayden Maiava to do his thing with the passing game. Kayden Dixon-Wyatt of USC will be a problem all nigth for the Penn State defense. Final score prediction: USC 27, Penn State 20 Player of the game pick: Jayden Maiava, USC quarterback Paul White, Contributor This hurts to predict, but I just don't see a way Penn State wins this game. The offense should be able to get back on track against a weaker defense, but if we couldn't stop Northwestern's offense, then I'm terrified to see what USC does. Final score prediction: USC 38, Penn State 27 Player of the game pick: Chase Sowell, Penn State wide receiver Christopher Sheppard, Contributor It feels like the gig is up for the Nittany Lions. What should be a celebration of one of college football's greatest modern traditions could turn into a State College massacre. I don't think that there will be much resistance from the blue and white, but I could see young edge talent Yvan Kemajou flashing some potential. away.blurb: STATE COLLEGE — USC freshman phenom Trent Mosley made his return for Saturday night’s White Out game against Penn State. Mosley, one of the No. 19 Trojans’ top receivers, missed the previous three games due to injury and was listed as a game-time decision on the Big Ten Conference pregame availability report. “He’s one of the best players on our team,” head coach Lincoln Riley said after the game. “You get one of those guys back, it's huge. He's a baller. He didn’t flinch. We've got a lot of trust in him, and he’s just a flat-out difference-maker on the field. There’s no other way to say it.” Treter has now missed two games due to an undisclosed injury, and it’s Paige’s first missed game of the season. The latter wasn’t even on the availability report until Saturday, when he was listed as a game-time decision. “It’s very different compared to the Coliseum, but it's definitely a lot of fun,” Chino resident and USC alumnus Sergio Hidalgo said. “Everyone's been really nice so far, and it being a White Out game makes it even more special because that's something we’ve always seen on TV with my wife and kids, so it's really cool.” Oregon’s duck mascot took a shot at USC during his pregame entrance before Saturday’s UCLA game. It entered Autzen Stadium inside a wooden Trojan Horse prop that had a red tongue comically sticking out of its mouth. The duck jumped out of the back of the horse with a sword and shield, with the song “Old Town Road” playing. It waved them around before running back into the tunnel. home.headline: Trent Mosley returns, revitalizes No. 19 USC against Penn State
home.blurb: STATE COLLEGE — USC freshman phenom Trent Mosley made his return for Saturday night’s White Out game against Penn State. Mosley, one of the No. 19 Trojans’ top receivers, missed the previous three games due to injury and was listed as a game-time decision on the Big Ten Conference pregame availability report. “He’s one of the best players on our team,” head coach Lincoln Riley said after the game. “You get one of those guys back, it's huge. He's a baller. He didn’t flinch. We've got a lot of trust in him, and he’s just a flat-out difference-maker on the field. There’s no other way to say it.” Treter has now missed two games due to an undisclosed injury, and it’s Paige’s first missed game of the season. The latter wasn’t even on the availability report until Saturday, when he was listed as a game-time decision. “It’s very different compared to the Coliseum, but it's definitely a lot of fun,” Chino resident and USC alumnus Sergio Hidalgo said. “Everyone's been really nice so far, and it being a White Out game makes it even more special because that's something we’ve always seen on TV with my wife and kids, so it's really cool.” Oregon’s duck mascot took a shot at USC during his pregame entrance before Saturday’s UCLA game. It entered Autzen Stadium inside a wooden Trojan Horse prop that had a red tongue comically sticking out of its mouth. The duck jumped out of the back of the horse with a sword and shield, with the song “Old Town Road” playing. It waved them around before running back into the tunnel. home.headline: Behind Enemy Lines: Penn State quarterback Rocco Becht is struggling
home.blurb: "Rocco Becht's sudden decline with his passing coincides directly with the loss of rising star receiver Koby Howard," McGuire told us. "Howard went down with an injury a couple of weeks ago and perhaps not so coincidentally, Becht became less effective. Not that he was lighting things up before that, but Howard was the big play guy to open things up for the rest of Becht's targets. It certainly is not a lack of chemistry as Becht's top targets are now all guys he was throwing to at Iowa State , but the efficiency is not showing. And he seems to succumb in pressure with Penn State down late in the last couple of games. His decision-making seems flawed in the crunch time, and that is worrisome." You can put the loss of Koby Howard up against the loss of Trent Mosley as a critical missing piece for each team's passing game and offense. Penn State really misses Howard. USC really misses Mosley. Finding other solutions and alternatives becomes paramount for each offense this coming Saturday. However, Jayden Maiava is definitely a better and more talented quarterback than Rocco Becht, and not by a small margin. Let's see if USC can take advantage of its clear-cut edge at quarterback.
